articleTitle: Extending the Frontier of ChatGPT: Code Generation and Debugging
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Large language models (LLMs), trained on vast corpora, have emerged as a groundbreaking innovation in the realm of question-answering and conversational agents. Among these LLMs, ChatGPT has pioneered a new phase in AI, adeptly handling varied tasks from writing essays and biographies to solving complex mathematical problems. However, assessing the performance of ChatGPT's output poses a challenge, particularly in scenarios where queries lack clear objective criteria for correctness. We delve into the efficacy of ChatGPT (GPT-4) in generating correct code for programming problems, examining both the correctness and the efficiency of its solution in terms of time and memory complexity. A custom dataset containing problems of various topics and difficulties from Leetcode has been used. The research reveals an overall success rate of 71.875%, denoting the proportion of problems for which ChatGPT was able to provide correct solutions that successfully satisfied all the test cases present in Leetcode. It exhibits strength in structured problems and shows a linear correlation between its success rate and problem acceptance rates. However, it struggles to improve incorrect solutions based on feedback, pointing to potential shortcomings in debugging tasks. These findings provide a compact yet insightful glimpse into ChatGPT's capabilities and areas for improvement.

articleTitle: Sensitivity of Lithium-Ion Battery SOH Estimates to Sensor Measurement Error and Latency
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Accurate and confident estimates of cell state of health (SOH) are crucial prerequisites to maximizing the performance and safety achieved from a battery pack. As SOH is not directly measurable, algorithms of varying complexity and computation cost are employed to provide SOH estimates. Input to these algorithms are the measurable quantities of the cell, acquired with sensor technology whose performances are defined by precision, accuracy and synchronicity. This paper provides an evaluation of the performance of SOH estimation algorithms against the integrity of the measurements provided by the sensors. Through execution of model-based simulation it compares the ideal case of zero sensor measurement error against real-life sensor performances which exhibit measurement offset, noise and nonsynchronicity. It considers typical usage scenarios in electric-vehicle and ESS applications, cell chemistry, estimation method and sensor performance. The measurements under examination are: cell temperature, cell voltage, and cell current.

articleTitle: Heartbeat Sound Analysis: Integrating Deep Learning Models for Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Heartbeat sound signal classification has been extensively researched in the field of medical signal processing, with various approaches proposed to address the challenges associated with accurate and efficient classification. The objective of this research is to develop an accurate and efficient heartbeat sound signal classification system using hybrid deep learning models. Various deep learning models including CNN, RNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, and GRU are compared with the proposed model. The performance of each model is evaluated based on the classification accuracy, and the results demonstrate that the proposed models achieve high accuracy rates. The hybrid model has been constructed by combining random forest (RF) with each deep learning model. The hybrid models outperform the standalone deep learning models, with RF+CNN achieving the highest accuracy rate of 94.43%, followed by RF+LSTM (94.38%), RF+GRU (94.09%), and RF+BiLSTM (93.85%). The proposed hybrid deep learning models provide a promising approach for the accurate classification of heartbeat sound signals, which has significant implications for early diagnosis and treatment of cardiovascular diseases.

articleTitle: Sensitivity of Lithium-Ion Battery SOC Estimates to Sensor Measurement Error and Latency
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Highly accurate and highly confident estimates of state of charge (SOC) are crucial prerequisites to maximizing the performance and safety achieved from a battery pack. SOC is not directly measurable, so algorithms of varying complexity and computation cost are employed to provide estimates of the values. Required inputs to the algorithms are the measurable quantities of the cell, whose performances are defined by precision, accuracy and synchronicity. This paper provides an evaluation of the impact on performance of SOC estimation based on the integrity of these inputs through execution of model-based simulation. It considers typical usage scenarios in electric-vehicle and ESS applications, cell chemistry, estimation method and measurement performance. The cell measurements under examination are: cell temperature, cell voltage and cell current. The cell model derivation and methods used in SOC estimation are described.

articleTitle: 80 GHz Phase Shifter in Liquid Crystal Compact Coplanar Transmission Line with Curved Bends
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This work proposes and characterizes a compact coplanar transmission line with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\circ}$</tex> curved bends for a liquid crystal-filled coplanar waveguide (CPW) continuously variable phase shifter up to 80 GHz. The device has <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\circ}$</tex> curved bends for the metalized core line, coplanar grounds, and coplanar channels that are filled with liquid crystals that can be adjusted in dielectric constants. The device with a reduced footprint achieves a differential phase shift of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$447.22289^{\circ}$</tex> at 80 GHz at the expense of 5.98894 dB insertion loss, i.e., <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$74.7^{\circ}/\text{dB}$</tex> in figure-of-merit (FoM). The added curved bend for miniaturization (as compared with the straight line-only design that is longer in size) exhibits a negligible difference in FoM for frequency bands lower than 20 GHz. As the frequency increases, the undesired curved bending effect on phase shift disturbance and insertion loss surge becomes more noticeable, and at 80 GHz, there is a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{\circ}/\text{dB}$</tex> decline in FoM (in comparison to the straight line-only design).

articleTitle: A Hybrid Security Algorithm for 5G-Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This paper addresses the security of an loT ecosystem where 5G plays a critical role in supporting the expansive Internet of Things (loT) ecosystem. The 5G-IoT ecosystem incorporates diverse applications such as smart homes, healthcare, agriculture, and transportation. However, the sheer volume of interconnected devices in this ecosystem poses significant security challenges, with the potential for dire consequences if breached, including endangering human life. The paper identifies key security features of 5G that can secure loT networks and explores specific security requirements and potential attack scenarios. It also outlines future research directions in this domain. Moreover, the paper proposes a hybrid security algorithm designed to enhance security within 5G-enabled loT environments. This algorithm incorporates a double Q-Iearning deep Neutron-based intrusion detection system (IDS), leveraging lightweight computation suitable for loT devices. Additionally, it integrates network slicing technology and Security-Aware Workflows (SAWS) to contain the impact of attacks and ensure business continuity. The proposed solution will undergo performance evaluation, with simulation results anticipated in future work. By addressing these challenges and proposing innovative solutions, the paper contributes to securing the evolving landscape of 5G-enabled loT ecosystems.

articleTitle: A Futuristic Optical and Wireless Convergence Network Towards 6G and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Emerging use cases and stringent requirements for 6G and beyond networks require new quantum leaps in mobile communication due to the demands of higher throughput, extensive bandwidth requirements, ultra-low latency and massive number of connected devices. The advancement in wireless communications and the advancement in optical networks will be essential in addressing the demands for future mobile networks by providing an innovative infrastructure for 6G and beyond networks. To support stringent requirements for 6G networks and beyond, new innovative technologies and systems are required that will combine optical and wireless networks. An innovative approach of converging optical and wireless networks promises to improve the network into new heights by creating a smart world with beyond-human cognitive communication capacity and speed, improved network scalability and enhanced energy efficiency. Research has shown that a promising architecture to achieve this goal, and cater for extremely high bandwidth and extremely low latency requirements is based on an All-Photonics Network. Therefore, in this paper, we propose an All-Photonics Network for the future to address bandwidth limitations, latency issues and massive connectivity. Furthermore, we propose an evolved infrastructure or architecture converging optical and wireless networks. Potential benefits for the evolved infrastructure are also discussed.

articleTitle: Attitudes Towards and Conditions to Use V2G Among Electric Vehicle Owners
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This study explores the secondary use of battery packs for electric vehicles in a vehicle-to-grid and vehicle-to-home context. The study conducted a literature review of the strengths and weaknesses of vehicle-to-grid and vehicle-to-home systems from the perspectives of different stakeholder groups. Based on the literature review, a survey was conducted in the spring of 2023. The study showed that vehicle-to-grid and vehicle-to-home technologies can provide the grid operator a way to balance the grid and cut peaks and pits caused by demand fluctuation. These technologies also present their own challenges, as an electric vehicle cannot be considered a permanent power source for the electricity grid. From the electric car owner's point of view, there is a monetary benefit from vehicle-to-grid use, as electricity could be sold back to the electricity grid and vehicle-to-home use would provide the average electric car user with electricity self-sufficiency for about two days. However, these benefits are overshadowed by the fear of the decay of the battery, as well as the increased range anxiety caused by the use.

articleTitle: Exploring Deep Learning and Machine Learning Techniques for Histopathological Image Classification in Lung Cancer Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: To diagnose lung cancer, this study thoroughly investigates the deep learning and machine learning methods used to classify histopathological lung cancer images. Using Dense-Net 121 for feature extraction, the study examines the effectiveness of several machine learning algorithms in this crucial medical task, including Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), AdaBoost, artificial neural networks, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and XGBoost. Most remarkably, the SVM algorithm is the most effective, with remarkable precision in training and testing. With a testing accuracy of 96.6 percent and a training accuracy of 99.99%, the SVM model specifically trained on features retrieved by Dense-Net 121 exhibits outstanding performance. Additionally, the SVM classifier demonstrates remarkable recall (96.40%), F1 score (96.39%), Cohen Kappa score (94.61%), and precision (96.39%), demonstrating its efficacy in correctly classifying histological images suggestive of lung cancer. These results highlight the possibility of combining SVM with deep learning-based feature extraction to improve lung cancer detection efficiency and accuracy, improving patient care and clinical decision-making.

articleTitle: Optimising IT Security Research via a Low Cost, Instantly Available, Cloud Based Cyber Range
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Testing the effectiveness of IT security measures for enterprises, companies, and institutions can often incur substantial costs in terms of time and resources. These costs encompass not only the investment in infrastructure for creating a cyber range but also the significant time and effort required to set up and configure the test environment. Similarly, academic researchers investigating IT security may find themselves dedicating as much time to preparing the test environment as they do to conducting the actual experiments. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a blueprint for a cyber range designed to replicate the IT environment of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) while incorporating the security provisions mandated by the Cyber Essentials standard. By leveraging cloud technology, enterprises and researchers can effortlessly create multiple instances of the cyber range in minutes, enabling them to focus on experimentation within a repeatable environment. Implemented within the SkyTap platform, the cyber range utilizes a private network segmented into multiple VLANs and supports various technologies and operating systems. Deployment of the cyber range is streamlined and repeatable, allowing users to initiate the process with a simple click. Additionally, a sharing portal can be generated to provide specific access to ethical hackers or penetration testers for collaborative testing. This blueprint has demonstrated its effectiveness, enabling our research group to establish multiple identical cyber ranges. These ranges were subsequently subjected to rigorous testing by ethical hackers to evaluate the efficacy of the implemented IT security provisions. The insights gained from this experimentation hold significant value for advancing research into the effectiveness of Cyber Essentials.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicles to Grid Technology-Load Flow Analysis Using Hybrid Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: For the successful integration of a number of electric vehicles (EVs) into the electric power grid, it is important to conduct comprehensive analysis and observation of the economic implications, operational benefits, and control advantages in ideal conditions. The observed trend indicates a progressive increase in the proportion of travel undertaken utilizing electric vehicles. Based on recent trends, it is anticipated that this particular mode of transportation will rapidly replace vehicles that are propelled by internal combustion engines. The objective of this research is to optimize power efficiency by minimizing power losses within the power system. This will be achieved by regulating the voltage levels within each bus to adhere to specific permissible limits. Additionally, the paper aims to ensure the system's radial architecture can support the anticipated grid modification caused by the integration of electric vehicles. In this investigation, a hybrid approach is used by combining Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Genetic Algorithm (GA), resulting in a novel artificial intelligence methodology. The analysis was performed using Matlab and a standard IEEE 33-bus transmission network to validate the proposed solution and assess its efficiency. The results indicate the feasibility of the proposed approach and illustrate its effectiveness in reducing power loss during individual operations, while also reducing processing time. Upon comparative analysis of the findings, it becomes evident that the hybrid genetic particle swarm optimisation (HGAPSO) algorithm yields a superior solution in comparison to the GA and PSO algorithms.

Author Keywords: Reduction of power loss and Electric vehicles

articleTitle: The Current State of The Art in VANET Simulation Tool Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Academic investigations into VANETs range back to the early 2000s. New protocols, technologies, and varied application scenarios have emerged in response to the potential for automobiles to communicate with one another through a wireless network. Many simulators were created because evaluating these research contributions using a real testbed presented significant challenges. New research problems on VANETs are emerging as a result of the rise of autonomous cars and the development of cutting-edge technology for example 5G and edge computing. So, it's important to take a second look at VANET simulations to see if they can still evaluate these new scenarios. In this work, we provide a comprehensive overview of the current status and capabilities of VANET simulators, demonstrating their use in evaluating innovative situations in VANET research. We use this analysis to highlight some of the most pressing questions that present and future VANET simulations will need to answer.

articleTitle: Control of Heat Exchanger Liquid Temperature Using PID Control and first Order Sliding Mode Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Nowadays, Heat exchanger systems are commonly employed in chemical plants due to their ability to maintain temperature and pressure within a broader range. The system transfers heat between two mediums while preventing them from mixing. It controls the liquid temperature inside closed processes, including large industrial systems. The problem encountered by heat exchanger systems is that they are prone to external effects like fluctuations in the surrounding temperature. These effects may disturb the system and lead to unsatisfactory results. This paper presents a solution to eliminating disturbances and noise signals, thus producing better results. Initially, a traditional PID controller was integrated into the system. The result obtained was different from what was expected. Then, the solution was sought in another controller, namely the sliding mode controller (SMC). SMCs have been found to work better than PID controllers, especially with non-linear systems, and they do not rely on system parameters. An SMC was designed and added to the system based on its advantages over PID controllers. The developed SMC showed better overshoot and settling time results than the classical controller. The system's response was improved, and the disturbances were eliminated. The design and evaluation of the controller were carried out using MATLAB Simulink software.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Differential Spatial Modulation over Rayleigh Fading Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Spatial modulation techniques have emerged as a candidate for fast and reliable wireless communications. However, most MIMO schemes require accurate channel state information (CSI) at the receiver, which can be challenging to achieve in practical settings with rapid channel variations or limited feedback capabilities. This paper proposes differential spatial modulation (DSM), a novel MIMO transmission scheme that eliminates the need for explicit CSI at the receiver. DSM achieves reliable data transmission without requiring perfect channel knowledge by encoding information in the spatial and signal constellation domains and exploiting the differences between repeated channel realizations. The DSM concepts are introduced, and analytical equations for the average bit error probability are derived over Rayleigh fading channels. Our study shows that DSM shows a better tradeoff between spectral efficiency (SE) and error performance, making it a promising solution for future wireless networks.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis and Attack Simulation on Quishing (a QC Code Phishing) using QRLJacker
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Quick response (QR) codes is a form of two-dimensional matrix barcode that can store information in a grid of black and white pixels which creates a unique pattern. The QR codes are usually scanned by mobile devices such as smartphones and will redirect the user's mobile devices to whatever URL the QR code contains. QR codes have grown in popularity due to their capabilities of redirecting to digital information or authenticating users [4]. This study implemented an explanatory research design. The study aims to describe, showcase, and investigate the different methods of quishing. To supplement the study, the researchers conducted a survey to better assess the knowledge of the peers around them. A survey was conducted to understand what the population thinks about QR codes and the underlying risks on its usage. The results of the QRJacking simulation were successful; the tool gained access to the target's Whatsapp. Outside of the success of the attack simulation, the research found that there were no restrictions when sending the Malicious QR code over messaging applications like Facebook Messenger, Discord, Whatsapp, and Viber. For future researchers, the researchers recommend using different apps, tools, and frameworks. Look into countermeasures and other methods of mitigation.

articleTitle: Deploying Wimax as a Backhaul Solution for Data Link Connectivity between Key Entities of Smart Grid Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: In this epoch the traditional old legacy Electric Grid has been evolved to Smart Electric Grid Communication Networks (SEGCN). Here the Smart Electric Grid Communication Networks (SEGCN) has attained a tremendous growth in terms of infrastructure development which includes well established data link connectivity between all key entities of Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Consumption. Hence as the Electric Grid has become smarter therefore a data link Communication network is required between all the key Entities of Generation, Transmission, Distribution and Consumption for bidirectional datalink connectivity. In this research, authors have recommended the deployment of WiMAX (3.5 GHz) licensed band as a Wireless backhaul technology for data link connectivity between Wide Area Network (WAN), Neighborhood Area Network (NAN) and Home Area Network (HAN) of Smart Grid Networks. In this research investigation Authors will put forward a better solution for data link connectivity between Smart Grid Entities by deployment of WiMAX Wireless Technology. Further Authors have simulated the RF Coverage area of WiMAX (3.5 GHz) Network, which corroborates to be an improved backhaul solution for Connectivity between the Wide Area Network (WAN), Neighborhood Area Network (NAN) and Home Areas Network (HAN) of Smart Grid Networks.

articleTitle: Quantifying Overfitting: Introducing the Overfitting Index
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: In the rapidly evolving domain of machine learning, ensuring model generalizability remains a quintessential challenge. Overfitting, where a model exhibits superior performance on training data but falters on unseen data, is a recurrent concern. This paper introduces the Overfitting Index (OI), a novel metric devised to quantitatively assess a model's tendency to overfit. Through extensive experiments on the Breast Ultrasound Images Dataset (BUS) and the MNIST dataset using architectures such as MobileNet, U-Net, ResNet, Darknet, and ViT-32, we illustrate the utility and discernment of the OI. Our results underscore the variable overfitting behaviors across architectures and highlight the mitigative impact of data augmentation, especially on smaller and more specialized datasets. The ViT-32's performance on MNIST further emphasizes the robustness of certain models and the dataset's comprehensive nature. By providing an objective lens to gauge overfitting, the OI offers a promising avenue to advance model optimization and ensure real-world efficacy.

articleTitle: Spectrogram and Mel-Spectrogram Based Dysphonic Voice Detection Using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: A non-invasive pathological voice detection system has been presented in this paper. This work considers two spectral images of voice signals namely spectrogram and Mel-spectrogram to detect dysphonic voices. The spectrogram is a convenient representation of voice signals on a time-frequency scale and has been popularly investigated in pathological voice detection algorithms. However, the spectrogram uses a linear frequency scaling and hence, does not consider the resolution of the human auditory model. The Mel-spectrogram overcomes this limitation by using a quasi-logarithmic frequency spacing. This work uses vowel samples available in the Saarbrucken voice database. The simulation results show that the Melspectrogram outperforms the spectrogram in terms of classification accuracy.

articleTitle: End-to-End Testbed and Simulation Framework for Examinations on System Performance and Cyber-Security in Digital Aeronautical Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The predicted growth in air traffic cannot be accommodated by current communication systems due to low data rates and cyber-security concerns. Together with new IP-based datalink options like L-band Digital Aeronautical Communications System (LDACS), the Future Communications Infrastructure (FCI) targets to overcome these issues. While the development and standardization of LDACS is already advancing, a co-existence with older systems like VHF Datalink is still required for a transitional phase. To study the performance of digital aeronautical communication systems from end-to-end, a testbed and simulation framework is proposed that combines several technical domains and provides an interface to test hardware. The concept, structure, elements, and status of the implementation will be presented as the testbed and simulation framework is still under development.

articleTitle: A Combined Single-Phase Boost Rectifier and DCDC Buck Converter into Three-Phase Open-Winding Machine Drive for EV Battery Charger
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This paper proposes a novel integrated battery charger for electric vehicles. The proposed system uses a three-phase open-winding machine drive system to perform the tasks of a single-phase AC boost rectifier and a DC-DC buck-boost converter. The charging circuit is realized by directly connecting the single-phase source to the middle points (a and b) of the open-winding machine and connecting the output (stator winding middle point c) of the parallel buck converter to the battery via a switch. In charging mode, electromagnetic torque and speed are canceled, and the motor acts as an inductor filter to handle the harmonic current on both the AC grid side and the DC-DC buck converter side. Additionally, by using interleaved techniques between parallel converters, a significant reduction in ripple of the AC grid current and DC-DC buck inductor current is observed, with THD lower than 5%. The proposed topology and control technique are described, and simulation results are given to validate the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Inverse Pendulum: Modeled by Associated Linear Equations ALEs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The inverted pendulum is modeled by Associated Linear Equations in its discrete version (Non-linear with Auto-Regressive inputs NARXs). Its homogeneous and particular response is evaluated by means of excitation of three harmonic components. The accuracy of its prediction is verified using the Volterra operators of 1st, 3rd and 5th harmonic order, the results show that the simulation is adequate to represent its non-linear response.

articleTitle: Efficient Semantic Relationship and Representation Reconstruction Based on Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Knowledge graph is pivotal in natural language processing, having reached a mature stage of development. They are comprised of interconnected synsets, forming a structured graph network with significant potential for leveraging in graph neural networks (GNNs). However, the extensive number of nodes within knowledge graphs often entails substantial computational demands during application. This study employs the GNNs to facilitate data reconstruction and dimensionality reduction. Inno-vatively, we utilize the Graph AutoEncoder (GAE) to introduce a fusion decoding approach, thereby implementing a dual decoding mechanism aimed at reconstructing intricate relationships and semantic features. Additionally, we employ an efficient multi-graph training methodology to mitigate the impact of complex structures on the training process. Our research contributes a novel solution for compressing and reconstructing knowledge graph data, fostering deeper integration between natural language processing and graph networks, and yielding promising outcomes.

articleTitle: A Study on Generating Cartoon Images Using Pixel Distributions Based on Cluster Classifications in CartoonGAN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) have brought significant advancements in the field of image transformation. In this paper, we propose a new approach to cartoon style image transformation by incorporating color quantization into the existing CartoonGAN model. The proposed method aims to maintain a more natural appearance compared to conventional methods by making it easier to preserve brighter colors over darker ones during the transformation into a cartoon style. This is achieved by understanding the RGB histogram of the original photograph to preserve color characteristics. Subsequently, the CartoonGAN process achieves natural cartoonization while preserving the image resolution and characteristics of the original image. This ensures a seamless and natural transformation without the dissonance often observed in previous cartoonization techniques, where the original image's colors may be distorted. The supporting dataset validates the superiority of this approach. We offer two assessments designed for human perception. PSNR indicates an overall improvement in image quality compared to conventional CartoonGAN, while SSIM demonstrates a significant enhancement in image quality. However, despite the effectiveness of this method, it faces limitations in producing degraded results depending on the distribution of the RGB histogram. Future research aims to address the limitations of color quantization and make further advancements in the field of cartoon style image transformation.

articleTitle: Comparator-Based Digitally Controlled Power Factor Correction Rectifier Using Digital Ripple Injection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Switched-mode power supplies under digital control typically require analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) for voltage and current feedback. Generally, the ADC conversion period extends with its resolution. High-power density and high switching frequency converters tend to use low-resolution ADCs to achieve shorter conversion periods. This paper proposes digital ripple injection to replace the ADC in digital power supplies with a comparator and a digital-to-analog converter (DAC). A power factor correction rectifier (PFC) is selected as the implementation platform due to its requirement to sense various signals, including AC grid voltage, high ripple inductor current, and DC output voltage. Experimental results are shown for a 500W boost PFC rectifier.

articleTitle: Maximum Power Point Tracker-Bus Voltage Controller Based on the Cascaded Buck-Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Non-isolated DC converters play a vital role when renewable energy resources are implemented. These devices are implemented in conjunction with control algorithms or control circuits like MPPT and feedback control. MPPT controllers are vital for retaining maximum power point operation for PV arrays. While feedback controllers are vital for regulating the bus voltage. This research aims to design an MPPT-Bus voltage controller that can be used in conjunction with a single directional DC converter that has no isolation circuitry. The proposed MPPT-Bus controller enables the PV arrays to harvest maximum power while regulating the bus voltage to 48VDC.

articleTitle: DDOS Attack Mitigation Based on FPGA Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: With the widespread use of computer networks daily, network security has become a significant problem in the new technology era. Due to the quick growth of the World Wide Web, it is becoming more challenging for researchers to find new methods to prevent attackers from reaching their targets. The spread of malicious cyber network activity poses a significant risk to numerous organizations and inflicts substantial economic consequences on society. Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) is a cyberattack technique that disrupts the regular traffic of the target server or system by flooding it with an abnormal flow of internet traffic from different sources. The current article explores the advantages of FPGA-based devices in network security to mitigate the effects of DDoS attacks.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based in Quantum Mechanics and Theorem of Bayes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid model of machine learning, based at the principles of quantum mechanics in conjunction to Bayes theorem. With such construction, it is tested onto a scenario dictated by the Mitchell criteria. By assuming stochastic system whose main dependence is through time, the proposed model exhibits a high experience probability just at the beginning of processes. The results of this paper would corroborate the hypothesis that stochastic system might be strongly dependent at the very beginning or initial conditions.

articleTitle: Noise-induced simultaneous firing in two leaky integrate-and- fire circuits with dead zones
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The enhancement of noise-induced synchronization in uncoupled leaky integrate-and-fire circuits by implementing dead zones was investigated. The dead zone is a time period in which the subsequent firing is inhibited and reduces individual firings of the circuits. Through numerical simulations and experiments involving white noise, it was demonstrated that the optimal dead zone width significantly enhances the rate of simultaneous firing. The results also suggest the importance of minimizing the mismatch in dead zone widths between circuits.

articleTitle: The nexus of cooperative learning and problem-based learning: A meta-analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Problem-based learning (PBL) is a student-centered method that develops critical thinking abilities. This study uses VOSviewer to perform bibliometric analysis on PBL research found in the Scopus database. An analysis of 317 articles and reviews revealed a steady increase in publications, with several authors became significant researchers, and the Journal of Engineering Education was a well-known publishing outlet. Higher education, critical thinking, collaborative learning, and active learning are the main topics of research. The paper illustrates new tendencies in research growth mapping from 1995 to 2024. These discoveries aid scholars, instructors, and legislators, directing subsequent PBL study and application.

articleTitle: A Cooperative Control Strategy for Wind Turbine-Grid Side Low Voltage Ride- Through Based on Novel Supercapacitor Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: In wind power all-direct current generation system, the wind turbines are boosted by DC/DC, collected and transmitted, and then connected to the grid through an inverter. When the grid voltage dips, the coordination mechanism of each controllable device in the system is not clear, and there is a surplus of active power, which in severe cases leads to the risk of the system going off-grid. To this end, a cooperative control strategy for wind turbine-grid side low voltage ride-through based on novel supercapacitor energy storage is proposed. During low voltage ride-through, the active output of the turbine is limited while boosting the reactive power injected into the grid by the grid-connected converter, and the unbalanced power in the system is absorbed using energy storage. Simulation results show that the proposed control strategy can effectively balance the power fluctuation of the system and improve the overall low-voltage ride-through capability of the system when a low voltage fault occurs in the AC grid.

Author Keywords: wind power all-direct current generation system

articleTitle: Domesticated Cat Activity Detection Using Deep Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Cats are one of the most well-known pet species worldwide. Cat owners take great care to ensure their feline companions' safety. Continuous observation of cats' behavior can help to assure their welfare. Due to the substantial benefits of sensor technology in the recent era, studies about activity detection have become very prominent. Applications for automated cat monitoring include monitoring and surveillance systems that accurately identify pets using deep learning methods for classifying pet activities. We can now use cutting-edge ways to get better results thanks to the technological revolution. Recently, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) has worked as a cutting-edge methodology for anomaly detection in manufacturing environments, sensor-based health monitoring systems, and signal processing-based systems. As compared to other models employed in the study for categorizing various types of activities, the CNN-LSTM architecture is seen to be the most effective. Additionally, it was discovered that all models outperformed their counterparts in data from the accelerometer, gyroscope, and magnetometer. The goal of this study is to use multi-axis sensor devices to identify ten pet behaviors, such as walking, running, eating, jumping, resting, etc. The approach for gathering data for this study involved 10 cats of various breeds, sexes (male=6, female=4), ages (age = 43), and the cats are small, medium, and large-sized in a safe setting. Following the data collection, the stages of data synchronization and data preparation were taken into consideration to eliminate unnecessary data from the dataset. We employed the class-weight technique to solve the dataset's imbalance issues. We used the class weight method to apply the LSTM algorithm. 99.45% training and 96.23% validation accuracy were displayed by the model using the class weight technique. The LSTM method will be useful for tracking cat behavior and for real-time activity monitoring.

articleTitle: Development of an Autonomous Navigation System for Small Vessels Using Remote Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Research on autonomous ships is being vigorously pursued globally. The International Maritime Organization (IMO) is leading a phased approach to the development of unmanned large ships. In contrast, the development of small ships is progressing independently in countries with a robust recreational maritime culture, focusing on innovative hull designs and systems. The small ship market is distinguished by high rates of used vessel purchases, a preference for cost-effectiveness, and a general lack of navigational aids compared to larger vessels. Furthermore, small ships are often operated by amateurs rather than professional navigators. These market characteristics suggest that the adoption of small autonomous ships will likely lag behind that of larger vessels. In response, our research aims to develop an economical program that enables autonomous operations in existing small ships or provides navigational assistance to inexperienced operators. Initially, we identified the necessary technology and economical equipment required to retrofit existing small ships for autonomous functionality. Subsequently, we analyzed the vessel's motion model to determine suitable control parameters. A straightforward control method was selected to facilitate user comprehension of the ship's status and interaction with the autonomous program. Our goal is to allow users to grasp the ship's motion dynamics through devices designed for autonomous navigation and to effectively implement navigational programs.

articleTitle: Comparison of Uncertainties in 2D LiDAR Mapping Depending on the Sensor Scanning Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Incorporation of 2D LiDAR (Light Detection And Ranging) sensors in indoor SLAM (Simultaneous Localization And Mapping) systems has become an increasingly common practice. The choice of these sensors is directly affected by the characteristics of the target environment. Among them, we may consider the scanning frequency of the LiDAR sensor. This paper analyses the influence of this parameter on low-cost 2D LiDAR sensors both from a computational standpoint and from the perspective of feature extraction in a mapping process. The experimental results suggest a relationship between the scanning frequency, the volume of processed data and the feature extraction uncertainty. It has been shown that lower scanning frequencies result in the detection of a larger number of features with reduced uncertainty.

articleTitle: Reduction of Distortions in Periodic Signals by Wiener Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Most of the techniques that are used to identify the I/O characteristic of a linear system require that it be stressed at the input through a periodic-type signal. The accuracy of the results is directly related to the degree of harmonic purity of the signal used as excitation. In this paper, a procedure is proposed for generating periodic signals whose degree of spectral purity is increased to extremely high levels using a procedure based on the Wiener filter. The procedure requires that the signal is generated by the usual procedure, and the subsequent filtering has such characteristics as to remove the harmonics that occurred and that decrease its spectral purity. The method does not act on the causes of generation of the additional harmonics, but removes their effects, restoring the signal to a very high degree of spectral purity. The proposed procedure is validated through examples to verify its effectiveness.

articleTitle: The Economic Impact of Load Shedding in Industry: A South African Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This research paper presents an economic analysis of the impact of load shedding on the South African industry, prioritising the related energy cost ramifications. Leveraging high-frequency operational and energy utilisation data collected over a month, this study envisions load shedding occurrences and assesses the scheduling impacts on businesses. It was established that utilising a diesel emergency generator incurs a 775 percent increase in operational energy costs during load shedding. The findings suggest improved energy management strategies during load shedding.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of IE4 Class Line-Start Permanent Magnet Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: LSPM motor has the starting characteristics of induction motor but permanent magnet is inserted. In the paper, the method of conducting analysis of LSPM motor is studied. Voltage equation is constructed on the basis of fundamental direct axis and quadrature axis. The value of current is calculated by voltage and torque equation. Then output torque at constant voltage can be obtained. The suggested analytical method can be faster analysis than FEA transient analysis. This analysis method will be useful for predicting motor performance.

articleTitle: Design of Remote Swerve-Drive Mechanism-Based Mobile Platform for Transportation Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Green energy has been attractive to researchers and engineers for decades to increase the utilization of renewable energy. One of the most widely applications is the electric vehicles and mobile robots. This study presents the design and implementation of a remote swerve-drive mechanism-based mobile platform namely S-bot. The S-bot is integrated with a set of solar panels to collect the radiation and store the energy in Lithium Polymer (LiPo) batteries. The S-bot prototype has shown extremely high maneuverability with no limitation in planar motion because it can move freely in translation, rotation, and a combination of both motion types simultaneously. Experiments of transporting a 15-kilogram payload in a range of 100 meters at a velocity of 1 m/s were conducted to test the performance. The S-bot has promising applications in many fields that require high maneuverability and high speed such as mobile robots, food delivery, package transportation in outdoor warehouses, large infrastructure buildings, agriculture, cleaning services, etc.

articleTitle: Forecasting Net Migration Rate Using Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This research enhances demographic forecasting by utilizing Support Vector Regression (SVR), a specialized implementation of Support Vector Machine (SVM), to precisely anticipate net migration rates. The approach highlights the examination of past data and other socio-economic and demographic indicators using SVR, showcasing its effectiveness in managing intricate data sets. The study emphasizes the utilization of sophisticated machine learning methods to enhance our comprehension of population dynamics and facilitate well-informed policy formulation. This work represents a notable advancement in the incorporation of state-of-the-art technology in the fields of demographic analysis and migration studies, providing accurate instruments for policymakers and urban planners. The work not only demonstrates the prediction capabilities of Support Vector Regression (SVR) but also establishes a basis for future research that combines SVM with other sophisticated analytical methods to achieve more robustness and comprehensiveness.

articleTitle: Enhancing Genomic Datasets with cGANs: A Study on Synthetic DNA Sequences for Non-Human Species
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: DNA sequences, unique to each species, are pivotal in life sciences. Despite their importance, genomic data analysis is hindered by limited availability, uneven distribution, and privacy issues, affecting the efficacy of machine learning in DNA sequence classification. This paper presents a new framework utilizing Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (cGANs) to synthesize DNA sequences and assess their resemblance to real sequences via supervised learning. This method enriches genomic datasets by modifying existing samples, reducing the need for new acquisitions. The research focuses on the black rat (Rattus rattus) and the chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes). By feeding real, synthetic, and hybrid DNA sequences into classification models, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Bagging Decision Trees, the framework illustrates that cGAN-generated synthetic DNA sequences can closely replicate the properties of real sequences, delivering comparable classification outcomes.

articleTitle: Policy Peek: Privacy Policy Automatic Analysis Tool
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: In today's digital world, websites often rely on personal accounts for user identification, which can inadvertently lead to sharing personal information without users' awareness. Legal requirements oblige websites to outline their data handling practices through privacy policies. However, these policies are typically complex and challenging for users to understand. Policy Peek: a novel browser extension proposed to simplify privacy policies. Policy Peek aims to utilize machine learning to analyze website policies. If the policy aligns with user preferences, seamless access is granted. Conversely, Policy Peek intends to provide simplified summaries and alert users if the policy fails to meet their preferences. Policy Peek strives to ensure internet browsing remains secure and privacy rights are upheld by empowering users to make informed decisions about their data.

articleTitle: Current-Mode Power-Line Signal Transfer for a Towed Active Sonar
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The work presented in this paper is focused on a towed active sonar that sends the received echo signal to the deck unit using the same power cable that powers the sonar. To ensure the signal is transferred with minimal noise, attenuation, and distortion over a long distance, a current-mode transmitter is used. The transmitter is designed to preserve the sonar signal waveform during transmission by a resonant current-feedback controller. The proposed circuit was tested in a sub-bottom profiling sonar with a 100-meter coaxial tow cable, and the transmission showed a flat magnitude response with low distortion. The gain differences are less than 0.33 dB, and the total harmonic distortion plus noise is less than 0.29% for the test signal frequencies from 3 kHz to 10 kHz.

articleTitle: Neural Network Based Model of a DC/DC Converter for Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The paper proposes a solution for modelling and controlling the operation of a DC/DC boost converter. The converter model is based on a neural network structure. The feedforward fully connected neural networks generate the appropriate model coefficients for the variable duty cycle. An optimal control approach is used for controlling the operation of the converter, and also reject external disturbances and return the system back to the steady-state regime. This approach will also be compared to the work of other authors which chose a Ziegler-Nichols controller. In the end, the paper will show that the chosen adaptive control strategy is also more energy efficient than a conventional control strategy.

articleTitle: Developed Deep Reinforcement Learning Model Based LSTM for Channel Approximation in PD-NOMA
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The significance of applying Deep Reinforcement Learning to approximate the channel weights for users in a Power Domain Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access is studied in this paper. In the proposed scenario, the deep Q network (DQN) procedure is developed and included into NOMA system where the suggested technique can be exploited to expect the channel weights for users. The aim of implementing the suggested DQN technique is to boost the sum rates for downlink communication and reduce the loss as well. To assure this target, the proposed DQN technique is prepared using parameters generated from simulations for different channel types, next the DQN scheme is modified via the collaboration with environment to generate the weights for channels related to users, then the estimated channel weights will be exploited at the receiver to retrieve the original information. Based on numerous performance metrics, simulation outcomes have confirmed that consistency is validated by the proposed DQN procedure when compared to standard benchmark schemes such as RL based Q procedure, DL based LSTM and typical MMSE technique.

articleTitle: Detection of Cyber-Attacks on the SMART GRID Using an Unknown Input Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The present work proposes an innovative method for detecting cyber-attacks in cyber-physical systems, focusing particularly on smart energy distribution networks. By utilizing unknown input observers, traditionally used for fault detection, this approach offers a promising solution to enhance the security of these systems against the growing threats of False Data Injection Attacks (FDIA). The proposed algorithm is based on the utilization of a bank of Luenberger-type unknown input observers. Simulations conducted in Matlab demonstrate the effectiveness of these attack detection and isolation algorithms, thus highlighting the significance of this contribution in safeguarding critical infrastructures.

Author Keywords: detection and isolation of an attack

articleTitle: Development of an Advanced Slip Control System for Enhanced Vehicle Stability: A Mathematical Modeling Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This article fits into the complex dynamics of Anti-lock Braking Systems (ABS) and the management of tire slide in current cars. ABS, a critical safety component, keeps wheels from locking when braking, maintaining maximum vehicle stability and control. We look at the basic concepts of ABS operation and how it might help reduce skidding incidents. Furthermore, we study several control systems for limiting tire slide, which is critical for maximizing vehicle traction and handling. We present a system that integrates ABS and slip control techniques using mathematical models, with the goal of improving safety and performance. Our studies demonstrate the efficiency of such integrated systems in reducing braking distances and boosting mobility under a variety of traffic conditions. In conclusion, we advocate for the widespread adoption of advanced ABS technologies coupled with robust slip control strategies to adopt safer driving experiences and reduce road accidents. Finally, we propose for wider deployment of modern ABS technology combined with strong slide control measures to provide safer driving experiences and minimize road accidents.

articleTitle: Precision and Versatility in Color Sensing: A Comprehensive Characterization of the TCS3200 Using Time Domain Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This study introduces an innovative approach to characterizing the TCS3200 color sensor through pulse coincidence techniques within embedded measurement systems, contrasting with benchmarks from professional-grade equipment. The investigation unveils the sensor's versatility in a broad range of applications, from environmental monitoring to health diagnostics, by leveraging frequency domain sensors for superior noise immunity and precision. Despite widespread utilization, a notable gap in methodological documentation, especially in frequency measurement, often leads to nonlinear responses at elevated frequencies. Through the development of a prototype allowing precise adjustments in color and positioning, alternative measurement methodologies are explored, aiming to enhance sensor characterization. Results, demonstrating a minimum relative error of 0.48 percent and an average error rate of 5.41 percent, underscore the method's efficacy, while also identifying opportunities for future improvements in accuracy, precision, and real-time data analysis. This research not only expands the TCS3200 sensor's applicability across various engineering disciplines but also lays the groundwork for further investigation into automatic measurement techniques and application-specific research, striving to surpass existing limitations and unlock novel possibilities in sensor technology.

articleTitle: A Comparative Assessment of the Temporal Fusion Transformer Model and Cloud-Based Forecasting Solutions in CPG Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Accurate forecasting is one of the most important factors for optimizing decisions ranging from retail to healthcare. There is a growing demand for innovative and powerful models. This paper enlightens the importance of this research particularly about the Consumer Packed Goods (CPG) sector. The Temporal Fusion Transformer Model differentiates itself from traditional statistical methods or cloud-based platforms by offering an interpretable and robust model that can take temporal relationships into account. The effectiveness of this model is demonstrated on real-world datasets, surpassing benchmark performances of cloud platforms such as A WS, and Azure even when considering the added complexity of holiday features or a custom solution.

articleTitle: Breaking the Excitation Chirp to Improve Ultrasonic Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Signal-to-noise ratio and axial resolution both play a primary role in ultrasonic exploration: the former is directly related to the depth of signal penetration in the innermost part of the subject under test. The latter improves with an increase of the bandwidth of the signal: this implies, however, an increase in the amount of noise superimposed on the useful signal. A tradeoff choice must be made between axial resolution (signal bandwidth) and maximum penetration depth (signal-to-noise ratio). The use of coded signals and appropriate signal processing techniques, as the pulse compression, overcomes this conflicting choice. Such use, although beneficial for the above aspects, implies that signals of relatively high duration are placed at the input to the measurement system, and this leads to an additional possible problem, related to overheating of both the object being measured and the transducer itself. The present work addresses this aspect concerning the use of coded signals and related processing techniques. By exploiting the linearity of the pulse compression procedure, a novel technique is proposed to deal with the problem of probe temperature rise in the case where very high penetration capacity and resolution are to be obtained while respecting the constraints imposed on temperature rise. The technique consists in fragmenting the Chirp signal into temporal parts, and then recomposing the signal through an appropriate processing technique. The simulation results reported show the validity of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Driver's Output Calibration Method with DAC Insertion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The driver's output calibration method with the help of a digital-to-analog converter (DAC), inserted in driver”s output, is presented in this paper. As interface speeds increase, it is essential to ensure that the IO drivers are properly calibrated with the transmission lines to prevent signal reflections. It is vitally significant to have highly accurate performance after calibration in high-speed systems which is difficult to provide. In the proposed method the equivalent PVT compensated rise and fall slew rates are provided due to the highly accurate R-2R DACs in order to avoid functional failures after transmission line. On top of that, the number of fingers of pre-drivers are decreased about five times owing to DAC insertion, so the overall area of the driver is decreased as well. Also, the data dependence jitter (ddj) is reduced. The proposed method can be used in special input/output circuits of several standards such as Double Data Rate (DDR), Universal Chiplet Interconnect (UCI), Universal Serial Bus (USB), and Peripheral Component Interconnect (PCI).

articleTitle: General Kinematics and Simulation for Mobile Robot Adapted Three Unconstraint Rollers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: In recent years, efficient mobility is required for omni-directional mobile robots in the logistics industry. There are various types of rollers mounted on mobile robots. Among them, omni-directional rollers (omni roller) are considered to have excellent omni-directional mobility and easy control. Assuming a circular mechanism, kinematics has been derived assuming an arbitrary arrangement along this circumference, and several studies have evaluated roller arrangements in terms of the speed efficiency of the driving rollers. To evaluate the roller arrangement, kinematics is necessary, in which not only the contact position of the rollers but also the direction is a parameter. In this study, kinematics is derived for a mobile robot equipped with three omni-rollers, with the contact position and direction of the rollers as parameters, and the behaviors of the roller velocity is investigated for the robot's movement in all directions.

articleTitle: Wind Turbine surface defects detection Based-on NasNetMobile architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: In this work a wind turbine defect detection solution based on a custom lightweight NasNetMobile model is proposed. Moreover, to understand the most important regions in our model prediction we used Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) as a model explicator, regarding to existing papers, this article focusses on interpreting result of a custom lightweight model (NasNetMobile) to understand and locate defected wind blade regions. However, Results showed that our custom NasNetMobile achieved good results with 93% of accuracy, adding that our custom model, as demonstrated by Grad-Cam, can identify the blade, and locate the defected region on it.

articleTitle: Investigating the Relationship between CrB Phase through Image Processing and Mechanical Properties of Metal 3D Printed Alloy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The relationship between the quantified CrB phase via image processing method and the mechanical properties of 3D printed SUS316L with boron was examined. Nine experimental conditions, i.e., boron content, feed rate, laser power, and scan speed, were designed by Taguchi method. The formation of CrB phase in 3D printed alloy with nine process conditions was quantified using image processing method. The image processing algorithm was based on the intensity difference between the regions of CrB phase and others. The CrB phase directly affects the mechanical properties of the 3D printed stainless steel. The quantity of CrB phase and mechanical properties depend on the processing conditions. The mechanical properties for tensile strength and micro hardness with processing conditions were measured. The same processing conditions were used for both quantification of the CrB phase and the mechanical properties test. The relationship between the quantified CrB phase and the mechanical properties was identified. As is generally known, a high amount of CrB phase deteriorates the mechanical properties of materials. Therefore, optimization of the processing conditions is crucially required to achieve the desired mechanical properties. With the signal the signal-to-noise (S/N) ratio analysis, the S/N ratio results for the quantified CrB phase were compared with that for the measured mechanical properties. The comparison through S/N ratio analysis contributes to determination of the influence of the CrB phase on the mechanical properties. Also, the comparison helps in finding of the desired mechanical properties.

articleTitle: Research on the Optimization of the Feeding Mode of the Pick-and-Place Robot Based on Supervised Learning and Stereo Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This study is to determine the optimal feeding mode for the tray input by stereo vision characteristics and supervised learning to identify the tilted and disordered workpieces. The 3D image correction of the Moire is applied to the calibration at different heights in the tray. The support vector machine method as supervised learning mainly leads to carrying out the optimal feeding mode for various input directions to object characteristics. The optimization will have different scores (identify the contour of the workpiece) and each feeding method can be analyzed to determine the best feeding mode according to the position, posture and contour. The method of depth scan calculation demonstrated that the classification on grouping SVM with 9 slices scan can resolve the depth resolution of 0.37mm. Searching the priority pick-and-place target can be determined by area size priority and area continuity priority. The goal is to find the object for the top and largest area every time. The optimization has different scores (area size and area continuity) to identify the contour of the workpieces and each feeding method can be analyzed to determine the best feeding mode (the left path).

articleTitle: Improving the Performance of Data Warehousing with Column Databases
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Databases have traditionally been used for different kinds of data, however, all have the same basic access patterns, known as online transaction processing (OLTP), that are similar to processing business transactions, such as making a sale, paying an employee's salary, or placing an order - the application most of the times looks up for only a small number of records then read, update, insert, or delete it based on user's input. However, as technologies grow, databases also begin to be increasingly used for another purpose - data analytics - whose query patterns are completely different from the former and demand a different approach. In this paper, we analyze the reason why traditional row-oriented databases, while can be used for both purposes, struggle the latter in terms of speed, and how columnar databases come out as a great solution.

articleTitle: Design of a Novel Z-Source-Based Bi-Directional DC Circuit Breaker to Improve Control Reliability
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The DC power system such as MVDC and LVDC is increasing due to renewable energy facilities such as solar power, fuel cells, and ESS (Energy Storage System). In addition, electric applications such as electric vehicles and electric propulsion ships are also increasing. DC circuit breaker that can protect these facilities and devices from electric shock has become an important issue. Recently, research on various forms of DC circuit breakers such as Z-Source structures has been actively studied. For example, coupled inductors and thyristors (SCRs) based on Z-Source structure have been previously proposed to reduce the parts of bidirectional DC circuit breakers. However, the conventional DC circuit breakers have problems such as control complexity and reliability. Therefore, in this paper, a novel topology of DC circuit breakers was proposed to improve control reliability. In this paper, the concept and operation principles were presented. In order to verify the proposed DC circuit breaker, an instantaneous failure experiment was implemented through scale-down testing of a rated ±10 A-class prototype.

articleTitle: Difussion-Weighted Images Analysis Using Regional Convolutional Neural Network for Stroke Lesion Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Stroke is a major type of brain disorder, and the MRI sequence known as diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) is often used to evaluate early changes related to strokes. Typically, stroke diagnosis requires manual assessment by neuroradiologists, which is subjective and time-consuming. Therefore, developing an automated stroke diagnosis system is crucial to streamline this process. This study presents a method for automatically detecting and categorizing stroke lesions using deep learning techniques applied to DWI. The dataset comprises 61 samples from Hospital Kuala Lumpur (HKL) and 69 samples from the public ISLES database, including acute hemorrhage, acute ischemic, chronic ischemic, and sub-acute ischemic strokes. The method employs a Regional Convolutional Neural Network (R-CNN) on DWI images, involving four stages: input image, region proposal network (RPN), computation of CNN features, and classification. Performance is evaluated using metrics such as accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. The technique achieves a classification accuracy of 64.62% with an average training time of 16.3 seconds. Overall, this stroke classification method shows promise for enhancing the diagnosis and categorization of brain stroke lesions using deep learning.

articleTitle: Optimizing Liquid Level Control in Double Tank Systems: A PID Controller Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The precise control of liquid levels in industrial processes is critical for maintaining productivity and product quality. However, dealing with liquid levels in double tank systems presents specific challenges due to issues such as cross-coupling and nonlinear dynamics. In this article, we consider a PID controller technique to improving liquid level management in double tank systems. The necessity of optimization in control systems, as well as the particular challenges presented by double tank structures are described. The PID controller is implemented as an adaptive tool for dealing with these challenges while highlighting its principles and features. The study digs into the process of system modeling, controller design, and double tank-specific optimization strategies. Throughout this work, there were investigated the challenges involved in maintaining liquid levels in such complex structures and proved the accuracy of PID controllers for overcoming all of these challenges. The obtained results are described through the accurate and stable control performance, regardless of dynamic operating environments and disturbances by utilizing PID control's adaptability and resilience.

articleTitle: Analytic Hierarchy Process of Digital Book Content Display Method on Large Displays
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The development of information technology and the digitization of books have led to the widespread use of electronic bookshelves that display a group of books on a display and the use of larger displays. In this study, we investigate the display method of digital book contents on a large-screen wall displays, an environment with few restrictions on the display size of book contents. We set up eight display patterns by combining four image display patterns that combine images of the front cover, spine, and back cover, and two image size patterns of actual and standard sizes. As a result of the pairwise comparisons with 52 participants, it was confirmed that the “Front cover and Spine” display method was highly evaluated by those who placed importance on the ease of identification.

articleTitle: A Rapid, and Low-Cost Electrical Impedance Tomography Sensor System for Non-Destructive Evaluation of Multiple Inhomogeneities
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Image reconstruction of the inhomogeneities is very important to evaluate the characteristics by creating multidimensional images using non-destructive measurements. The reconstructed image with the lowest possible noise is desirable in order to maintain a good resolution and high accuracy. This paper presents an approach to reconstruct and evaluate the multiple inhomogeneities by utilizing non-invasive and non-destructive measurements considering an Electrical Impedance Tomography <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{EIT})$</tex> sensor system. A high-precision sensor using an array of electrodes in a cylindrical structured domain is designed for multidimensional measurements of non-conductive, bio-, and conductive inhomogeneities. The impedances at frequencies up to 100 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{kHz}$</tex> are measured and the accuracy is evaluated. The reconstruction analysis is performed successfully using a complete electrode model with the help of impedance difference method considering finite element method (FEM) modeling. A noise controlled hyperparameter value ranges from 0.0097 to 0.57 in addition with the type, position, and size of the inhomogeneity is considered in the analysis.

articleTitle: Cognition in Human Computer Interaction: Toward Measures of Usability
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This study developed a framework for predicting usability factors through an understanding of how cognitive traits relate to human interaction with a computer system. Specifically, this study examined the relationship of field-independence, spatial visualization, logical reasoning, and integrative reasoning to interaction process and outcome. The research hypothesis was tested through correlation to determine the relationships among variables. As a post hoc analysis, multiple regression analysis was used to examine the predictive power of four cognitive variables on interaction outcome. The results of the study emphasize the importance of considering cognitive variables as important predictors to human interaction process and outcome.

articleTitle: On Security Level of Some Secret Keys of Concealing - Restoring System Aimed to BCI/BMI Security
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: We study the concealing-restoring system (CRS) for analog signals. CRS conceals any analog signal using some random-noise disturbances, and splits it into some concealed signals. CRS restores the signal from those concealed signals using a proper noise filtering. In this paper, a kind of security level of CRS is briefly reported. CRS has several secret keys; a tendency of the security level is investigated for some of them through the several numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Movement-Based Human-Machine System Using Arduino and Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Disabled people with quadriplegia caused by a cervical spinal cord injury, cerebral palsy, or stroke can greatly benefit from hands-free control methods to reduce their level of dependence on daily activities. In hands-free control solutions, the head movement-based control has proven to be the most efficient, natural, and comfortable way to convey desired commands to activate home appliances and access assistive devices. This study aims to develop a hands-free human-machine system (HMS) for quadriplegic people. The system is developed using an ADXL335 accelerometer and an Arduino Uno board, which is reasonably compatible with deploying a feedforward neural network (FFNN) for effectively detecting the intentional head movement.

articleTitle: Simulation and Analysis of Bidirectional Charger in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology has gained traction due to the shifting market dynamics towards electric vehicles (EVs). With the surge in EV adoption, there's a growing interest in charging-related discussions. The necessity for a bidirectional charger, achievable through V2G technology, has become apparent. Such a charger enables power movement among the vehicle battery and power grid, enhancing power stability by facilitating load leveling, peak load saving, and voltage regulation. Implementing V2G requires a dedicated vehicle battery charger capable of supporting bidirectional power flow. This paper proposes a novel approach to controlling bidirectional battery chargers, applicable for both charging and discharging in V2G and grid-to-vehicle scenarios. The performance of the bidirectional charger is evaluated using MATLAB Simulink modeling for both charging and discharging modes, with results visualized to illustrate effectiveness.

articleTitle: Assessing the impact of Digital Elevation Model resolution on Elevation Gain Estimations in Trail Running
