publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of accurately estimating Elevation Gain (EG) in trail running using GPS devices, where resolution of Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) plays a critical role. We propose an algorithmic enhancement to increase the resolution of a 4m DEM to 20cm, aligning it closely with high-resolution LiDAR models. Quantitative analyses reveal that this method significantly improves EG estimations, demonstrating a considerable reduction in error margins compared to conventional EG estimation using raw GPS. Specifically, our findings indicate that the bilinearly interpolated DEM achieves near-LiDAR accuracy at 20cm resolution, with error rates markedly decreasing at this scale. This study underscores the potential of using enhanced-resolution DEMs as a cost-effective alternative to LiDAR, particularly in applications like trail running where precise elevation data is crucial. Our approach not only offers a substantial improvement in the accuracy of physical workload assessments but also enhances the accessibility of high-quality elevation data for broader geographical and environmental applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Dehumidification Efficiency in Desiccant Systems Using Non-Corrosive Ionic Solutions and Recirculation Air Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This study investigates the impact of utilizing non-corrosive ionic solutions in an enhanced adiabatic liquid desiccant dehumidification system, focusing on the dehumidification process with fixed solution flow rates and air volumes for both dehumidification and regeneration. The air intake modes for the dehumidifier tower are set to outdoor air, while the regenerator tower compares outdoor air with a recirculation air mode. The study examines the influence of different air intake modes on dehumidification efficiency. Data from the experiments were solved using engineering equation-solving software. When the moisture content of the ambient air is 14.5g/kg changing the air intake mode from outdoor air to regeneration with recirculation air decreases the outlet dew point temperature from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$11.7^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8.82^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, the outlet humidity ratio from 8.59g/kg to 7.07g/kg, and increases the dehumidifier capacity from12.76kg/h to 16.05kg/h ‘, with the energy factor (EF) improving from 1.8 to 2.5. The experimental results indicate that employing a recirculation air mode in the regenerator tower achieves superior dehumidification performance.

articleTitle: City Road Condition Evaluation Through Artificial Vision Information When Driving: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The condition of urban roads is a major concern for many city councils, as it directly impacts the safety of both vehicles and pedestrians. Maintaining roads in optimal condition necessitates regular and thorough inspections, which can be both costly and resource-intensive. This study introduces a novel approach to monitoring road conditions by employing a fusion strategy that combines camera and instance segmentation techniques, enabling precise pothole identification and mapping within the urban landscape. In our research, we have evaluated the performance of four iterations of the YOLO (You Only Look Once) algorithm (YOLOv5, YOLOv6, YOLOv7, and YOLOv8) for the detection and characterisation of potholes. The systems were trained using publicly available datasets. Our findings reveal the strengths and weaknesses of each YOLO version in pothole detection tasks, with a surprising outcome: YOLOv5 demonstrates superior performance over its more recent successors. This work not only provides a feasible solution for continuous and automated road condition monitoring but also offers a comparative analysis of cutting-edge detection technologies, contributing valuable insights for future urban infrastructure maintenance strategies.

articleTitle: A Study on Performance Improvement of CartoonGAN through Reflective Object Removal for Comparative Analysis of Content Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Due to the development of generative artificial intelligence and various application possibilities, life can be changed more productively and creatively by supplementing human labor. CartoonGAN can reduce labor and costs through image generation by transferring an artist's cartoon style. In this process, a limitation of the generated image occurs according to the light of the input image. In order to create a more unique artist's style, the reflection of light in the input image must be controlled, and research that maintains detailed information should be conducted. Therefore, in this study, we aim to improve the performance of cartoon image generation by proposing algorithms for improving resolution and controlling the reflection of light.

articleTitle: Voltage and Load Profile Analysis for a Grid System with Incorporation of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Significant economic and operational benefits and control advantages under ideal conditions must be analyzed and observed before a large number of Electric Vehicles (EVs) can be successfully integrated into the electric power grid. Incorporation of EVs to the power network can cause problems in system parameters like voltage instabilities and power losses. This research aims to keep the systems in good working order so that they can expand to accommodate the addition of electric vehicles to the grid while still limiting the power lost by the system and staying within the permitted voltage range for each bus. In this study, two distinct artificial intelligent (AI) methods we combined to create a genetic algorithm particle swarm optimization (GAPSO) method. The effectiveness and viability of the suggested method were analyzed with the use of Matlab in a typical IEEE 33-bus Transmission network. The results validate the effectiveness of the suggested approach and show that it reduces the amount of power lost during separate runs while concurrently decreasing processing time. When looking at the results side by side, it's evident that hybrid genetic algorithm particle swarm optimization (HGAPSO) delivers a better solution than both genetic algorithm (GA) and particle swarm optimization (PSO).

Author Keywords: Power Loss Reduction and Voltage Profile Improvement

articleTitle: Evaluation of Improved Transient Behaviour of Single Wire Earth Return under 22 kW Motor Starting Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: A Single Wire Earth Return (SWER) is a distribution system that supplies power to rural areas or farms. The cost-benefit of implementing this distribution system yields a third of the cost compared to the traditional three-phase distribution system. The types of loads a SWER line is designed to supply are domestic loads, which are mainly resistive loads. A 22-kW motor during starting conditions is not resistive but is predominantly inductive; furthermore, the motor creates transients on the line it supplies. An experiment was conducted to determine Single-Phase Induction Motor (SPIM) parameters. These tests were performed following the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers standards under two different running conditions: a no-load (light) test and a load (locked rotor) test. MATLAB, SimPower Systems software were used to simulate the transient behavior of the SWER line under starting conditions. The study has concluded that a SPIM connected at the end of a SWER line will lead to a large voltage depression on other healthy loads. There are numerous ways in which a consumer can enjoy the benefits of the SWER system that are recommended and the cheapest method is suggested in this paper. Utilities, government departments, scholars and consumers need to be educated about this electrification method, particularly in South Africa where the SWER line is considered an inferior power supply.

articleTitle: Accurate Estimation of Circuit Process Variations Using an On-Chip Process Monitoring Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: With the scaling of CMOS technology below 100-nm, it has become increasingly crucial to monitor the performance of MOSFETs early in the process cycle. Die-to-Die process variations can occur during the production cycle of a silicon wafer and can cause mismatches in electrical parameters of MOSFETs thereby impacting their frequency and leakage power. Inaccurate estimation of electrical parameters due to process variations can result in a greater model vs silicon mismatch and can lead to significant overdesign of a circuit and poor yield. This paper proposes an on-chip process monitoring sensor to monitor and track the process deviations of standalone semiconductor devices which constitute the chip. The sensor consists of multiple test structures of varying oxide thickness, channel width and length to cover a sufficiently large design space for impactful results. Several key parameters including the threshold voltage and current gain for MOSFETs, the base-emitter voltage for BJTs and resistance for polysilicon resistance are extracted. The proposed on-chip process monitoring circuit significantly reduces the test time and data post-processing by using the constant current methodology for measurements. It also overcomes the shortcomings of scribe line-based process monitoring test structures by having a better coverage of the device types used inside a chip, offering the circuit designer a better understanding of the process centering and the capability to monitor electrical parameters of circuit IPs throughout their production cycle. Detailed SPICE level simulations and Silicon analysis conducted on 40-nm bulk CMOS technology demonstrate the effectiveness of the on-chip process monitoring sensor.

articleTitle: Vehicle Connectivity Analysis in Delay Tolerant Network for Different Antenna Ranges
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Vehicular Adhoc Networks (VANETs) are the op-portunistic networks (OppNets) which use connectivity issues as a chance. A VANET, categorized by connectivity disruptions, is well suited because of rapid vagaries in network scenario, variable vehicle density, and high vehicle speeds. In this paper, the vehicle connectivity in Delay Tolerant Networking (DTN), a connection less data transmission model that utilizes intermittent connections and OppNet to transfer information, for different antenna ranges is analysed. A variety of simulations were performed to determine the connectivity with different DTN protocols and vehicle conditions for various antenna ranges. As a result of the simulations, the source spray and wait (SSNW), binary spray and wait (BSNW) and First Contact (FC) protocol give better performance metrics for different vehicle antenna ranges in low and high-density scenarios.

articleTitle: Classification of Critical Stages of Damage by Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: It is essential for estimating the failure of metallic components and to classify the faults on a real-time basis in process monitoring for the better product quality of a metal specimen; so that the location and detection of a specimen's damage can be known to minimize the production cost. This research provides a novel approach to using the Acoustic Emission (AE) parameters for the classification of damage failures in metallic specimens using support vector machines (SVM). The developed SVM model classified the stages of deformation/damage such as elastic, plastic, necking, and fracture in a dog bone(metallic) specimen using the AE data gathered. Different classification methods were used, such as decision tree, K-Nearest Neighbors, Linear Discriminant Analysis, Boosted Tree, Naïve Bayes, and multi-kernel SVM. It is found that SVM-based classifier results are satisfactory as the trained quadratic SVM model could classify the damage stages correctly with 98.3 % accuracy for given datasets in the training stage. The performance of the quadratic SVM model was evaluated using the confusion matrix. The proposed SVM model contributed promising results when compared with the actual data. The prediction of the deformation stage may help to know the criticality of failure, which can help take necessary actions to increase the life span of the metallic specimens.

articleTitle: AI Ethics in IoT: Involving Society in the Discussion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: For all areas that use Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Autonomous and Intelligent Systems (A/lS), including IoT, recent discussions in the global media about the effects of AI chatbots, such as the OpenAI ChatGPT and Google Bard tools, on education, fraud, and even the disappearance of some professions are a warning. Therefore, we need to talk to society about the use of AI to avoid unfounded rumors that could hinder the development of IoT technologies that use AI. In this article, we propose to discuss with society projects that use AI or A/lS technologies, including IoT devices, following the General Principles of IEEE Ethically Aligned Design, to obtain society's support for these technological advances and avoid rumors and false information that could harm them.

articleTitle: On Digital Art Generation Using Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Art has cultivated human imagination across cultures for centuries. The peak of human creativity is fully expressed by artists through artworks. With technological advancement, researchers have pondered over the possibility of teaching computers to create arts. Although earlier computer arts were uniform and lacked creativity, there has been a recent shift in computer arts with the introduction of generative adversarial networks (GANs). GANs have generated photo-realistic human faces and other images that are virtually indistinguishable from real images. Although GANs have been used to generate various art forms, including cartoons and NFTs, their application to abstract and landscape or nature arts have been limited. This paper evaluates and compares two arts generation models through an end-user survey. It explores the possibility of GANs in generating abstract and landscape arts by using two different GAN architectures. Results from a case study indicate that the GAN generated artworks are more interesting to the volunteers than those generated by real artists. The GAN generated artworks are also on part with the real artworks in terms of overall quality.

articleTitle: Perspectives on Employing Physics-based Battery Management for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Mathematical models of lithium-ion batteries assume numerous forms, exist on a variety of scales and serve many different purposes. Unlike empirical circuit-based models, those built from fundamental electrochemical principles harbor essential information that can be exploited by advanced battery management algorithms to push battery performance and lifetime close to theoretical limits. While useful, physics-based models (PBM) are commonly avoided because they are conceptually and computationally complex, and are often seen as unworkable for engineering applications. However, by utilizing simplified forms of PBMs, these challenges can be overcome. This paper presents and demonstrates by example a practical approach to the design of battery management algorithms for the important cases of (i) fast-charge and (ii) state-of-power estimation that employ reduced-complexity PBMs. It further highlights the challenges pursuant to applying these methods and points the way for future improvements.

articleTitle: Enhancing Profitability through AI-Optimized Accounts Receivable: Reducing Cash Conversion Cycles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The management of accounts receivable is crucial to a company's profitability and overall growth, as it directly influences financial performance. Specifically, firms with longer cash conversion cycle periods exhibit lower profitability compared to those with shorter cash conversion cycle periods. The processes involved in this domain are often laborious, time-intensive, and susceptible to mistakes. This research paper aims to improve efficiency of accounts receivable procedures across various industries, ultimately enhancing the daily operations of collectors and reducing the cash conversion cycle. The proposed solution consists of a comprehensive architecture which leverages Generative AI to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of accounts receivable processing. Additionally, it addresses challenges such as customer segmentation, credit management support, collector assistance, dispute verification, and the customization of emails in accordance with customer strategies. Integration of Langchain-based QA system further enhances and optimizes the business operations.

articleTitle: An Additively Manufactured 3D Printed Electronics System for Personalized ear-EEG
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This paper introduces a 3D-printed ear-EEG device that is manufactured in a personalized way using an electronic additive manufacturing approach to print the entire system. The system's microcontroller is also considered to enable the potential for a fully wireless Bluetooth signal transmission. Leveraging 3D-printed electronics technology, the device can be customized and printed to fit an individual's ear anatomies and shape, ensuring optimal contact and signal acquisition. The device underwent various tests on one subject, including Auditory Steady-State Response (ASSR), Alpha Modulation, Active Oddball (P300), and Passive Oddball (MMN) to demonstrate the proof-of-concept. Results indicate the device's capability to capture EEG signals from steady-state and transient stimuli, showcasing its potential for versatile applications in neurophysiological monitoring or brain-computer interface (BCI) applications. The ear-EEG device could in several aspects, be comparable to traditional scalp EEG, highlighting its promise for advancing neurophysiological research and clinical applications.

articleTitle: Simulation and Analysis of BIPV Solar Panel Configuration on Building Facades
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: To address environmental degradation and energy scarcity, developing diversified autonomous energy sources is crucial. The advent of Building Integrated Photovoltaic (BIPV) systems allows for the incorporation of photovoltaic modules into building exteriors, creating integrated solar systems. This study aims to enhance BIPV system efficiency on facades through simulation and analysis, evaluating various environmental conditions quantitatively and qualitatively. By considering installation costs, energy efficiency, and user demand, the research proposes optimal BIPV configuration strategies. The objective is to resolve previous BIPV design and integration challenges, establishing an effective BIPV design planning model for optimal simulation and analysis.

articleTitle: Development of IoT-Based Smart Home Automation System with Open-Sourced Components
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Smart home systems aim to provide more accessible and easier services such as security management, lighting, savings, and daily life needs by using wireless communication standards and tools. This study aims to propose a low-cost and open-sourced smart home automation system using the Internet of Things architecture by integrating motion, gas, and heat sensors into Arduino Mega and mobile applications. During the system design process, we preferred sensors that adopt low energy consumption features and allow real-time data to be transferred from residences to homeowners. Obtained raw data from the home environment through sensors is visualized with the IoT analytics function in the system and delivered to the homeowner in the form of a report via the mobile application. After programming essential functions and modelling prototypes, we conducted feasibility techniques using simulation and peer-review performance tests. The test results show that smart home automation systems can be developed using open-sourced sensors and integrated into IoT Analytics platforms and mobile applications. We believe that the proposed system will positively contribute to their literature in the context of integrating IoT analytics and mobile application support and make homeowners' control of their residences easier.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Antenna Array with Undefined Mutual Coupling via Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Failure of element (s) in Antenna array degrades the performance of the radiation pattern, and consequently affect mobile communication systems. Hence, diagnosis of antenna array is an important operation whenever element (s) failure in the array occur. There are various diagnostic techniques found in literature that employ compressive sensing. Conversely, the techniques are based on easy formulation of array factor with no incorporation of mutual coupling existing between the radiators. This article shows how this deficiency lead to defective and bad diagnosis when there is presence of mutual coupling using port-level coupling matrix and average embedded antenna pattern. Furthermore, the element excitations are optimized to reduce the effect of mutual coherence of system measurement matrix, causing reduced measurements required for effective fault detection. Numerical simulation and experimental results demonstrate how the incorporation of mutual coupling generates an adequate and reliable array diagnosis. Finally, the implementation of the proposed framework via measurement probe in space shows motivating results for its practical applications.

articleTitle: Temperature Control In A Rotary Hearth Furnace Using AI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Industrial furnaces are often used in siderurgy and metallurgy applications. Most of them are based on burning different fuels or use electrical resistors to bring the temperature to the desired working conditions. This paper aims to show a possible approach of an adaptive controller implementation using neural networks to reduce the gas consumption of industrial furnaces. The neural networks generate the appropriate coefficients, both for the transfer function and the controller, with respect to the variation of the gas flow.

articleTitle: Transmission Expansion Power Planning With Renewable Energy Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: To satisfy the increased demand, renewable energy (RE) integration should be the ultimate objective in extending transmission lines as it contributes to minimizing gas emissions and is environmentally beneficial. Electric distribution network planning involves improving the system to meet demand and limits most cost-effectively. The importance of expanding the transmission network cannot be overstated. Transmission Network Expansion Planning (TNEP) is a periodic necessity driven by dynamic civilizations with increasing energy demands. This study utilizes the Vuyani-Eros 150km, 400kV transmission line in South Africa, which is integrated with the Metro wind farm situated in the eastern cape. The findings of this research indicate that connecting renewable energy sources (RES) to the transmission line to increase power access in the transmission is, in fact, advantageous as it will increase power access with environmentally friendly power. This research further suggests utilizing optimization approaches to identify the optimal place for transmission extension, particularly as the system increases in size and complexity.

articleTitle: Investigation of Training Effects and Entertainment by Job Motion Training Tidy-up Games
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Current job (vocational) training faces issues such as a shortage of instructors, lack of training equipment, and aging of instructors. Tidying up is a necessary action in daily life and social life, but many people are not good at it. In this study, we propose a VR tidying-up game using HMD and Unity. We clarify the difference in entertainment value and training effect from the tidying-up PC game and investigate the effectiveness of the VR tidying-up game.

articleTitle: The Technological Disruption Caused by the Composite Insulator Crossarm in the Electrical Energy Transmission Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The newest disruptive technology in electrical energy transmission lines is the use of composite materials in the towers. This includes composite insulator crossarms. The possibility on reduction of towers, lower clearances, compacting lines, makes this novel technology attractive to transmission line designers. These changes in tower design not only transform the infrastructure but also technical requirements, leading to significant impacts on the sector's supply chain. A notable advantage of this technology is the ability to solve the persistent issue of bird droppings on insulator strings.

articleTitle: Exploring Delay Tolerant Network: A Simulation Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This paper provides an in-depth exploration of Delay Tolerant Networks (DTNs), focusing particularly on the development and functionality of High Delay Tolerant Networks (HDTNs). The distinction between DTNs and HDTNs is illuminated, emphasizing the greater resilience and performance of HDTNs. The role and significance of HDTN simulators were thoroughly explained, explaining their essential role in modeling, and predicting the behavior of these advanced networks. A detailed walkthrough is offered on the installation, configuration, and simulation process of the HDTN Simulator, making this study a valuable resource for practitioners in the field. The paper also incorporates the use of DTNSim to further extend the simulation capabilities of HDTNs. The research also delves into the results and network topology obtained from the simulation, offering valuable insights into the practical applications and implications of HDTNs. The findings contribute to a growing body of knowledge surrounding the design, implementation, and management of high delay tolerant networks, thereby aiding future developments in this critical aspect of network engineering.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity Compliance Tests for Smart Electricity Meters in Smart Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Ensuring cyber security is crucial in a smart distribution system, mainlyin relation to smart electricity meters. As smart meters play a pivotal role in modern energy infrastructure, conducting thorough testing is important to evaluate their ability to withstand potential cyber threats. These compliance tests contribute to enhancing the overall cyber security posture of the Smart Distribution System, ensuring the integrity, confidentiality, and reliability of smart electricity meters in today's dynamic cyber security landscape. As part of product security, according to the IEC 62056 series, smart meters offering three authentication mechanisms at different security levels: lowest level, low level, and high level. This paper provides a comprehensive understanding of DLMS/COSEM security authentication for smart meters. As part of smart meter security, the authors simulated various authentication mechanisms available in DLMS to ensure the proper implementation of security measures in smart meters. Validating the security mechanism before installing the smart meter in the field is essential for protecting against cyber attacks.

articleTitle: Econophysics Through Quantum Mechanics: Inflation as a Perturbation of Consumer Price Paths
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Since inflation is mainly characterized by the abnormal behavior of binomial of economic variables constituted by consume price index and purchasing power, this paper has applied a quantum mechanics model to explain the erratic rising of consumer price index in time. In concrete, the time evolution operator has been projected onto a scenario of consumer price index. Thus, it has been hypothesized that inflation might be boosted by the apparition of non-visible interactions at the control and management of economy policy of a country. The case of free particle as commonly used in physics has been employed. Here, the Hamiltonian has been added an extra operator that would cause nonlinear trajectories of consumer price index in time. From the theoretical results and their interpretations, it is argued that unexpected factors far away from macro-economic as well as micro-economic dynamics would fit well with the trigger of inflation. The present theoretical approach explains the curve of inflation of energy price at Eurozone between 2020 and 2022 yielding a certain level of coherence.

articleTitle: BuyLow: A Platform Design for Online Goods and Services Trading Platform in the Philippines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This study focuses on the business design model covering the creation and developing the BuyLow: Goods and Services Trading Platform in the Philippines. BuyLow aims to provide an alternative e-commerce approach to typical marketplace where customers meet to exchange their goods and services without any currency. In a common scenario the amount goods and services purchased are also paid by manufactured goods or offered services. BuyLow offers exchange of goods and services in a much safer and reliable way. Buylow also offers a platform where people can trade not just physical product but also digital services such as animations, video editing, digital art and other modern digital products that can be stored electronically. BuyLow can be a game changer in the e-commerce industry in the Philippines because it utilizes unused item from each user in exchange for possible useful items from other users. The BuyLow business model is based on subscription and advertisements. For free users they can only post up to 4 items per day and can transact up to 8 trades per day, after the quota (for free users) certain features will be disabled such as ability to post item for trade, accept trade proposal or submit trade proposal to other users, but can also do monitoring of exisiting trades. BuyLow can be a game changer in the e-commerce industry in the Philippines because it utilizes unused item from each user in exchange for possible useful items from other users. With the use of AI and Machine Learning the success of the system can be greatly improve by producing new and accurate data about the system environment.

articleTitle: Designing a Naturalistic Driving Situation Extraction Method to Improve the Learning Process of Automated Driving Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Diverse and realistic traffic scenarios are critical to evaluating the AI safety of automated driving systems in simulation. The existing methods for learning automated driving AI are mainly based on rule-based heuristics or real-world-based iterative experiments. However, these methods have limitations in that they are difficult to prepare for unpredictable situations and are costly and time-consuming. In response to this, this research proposes a new method for learning and validating automated driving AI based on data obtained from real-world road environments by utilizing a digital twin environment. This is an early stage of research that aims to automatically generate realistic and varied traffic scenarios that learn from naturalistic driving data. The proposed technique is validated through situation extraction and analysis based on real-world road data, which accurately simulates realistic road conditions to ensure safety while saving cost and time. This approach can alleviate the anxiety of automated driving technology and open up the possibility of new learning methods.

articleTitle: Optimized Routing in FANET Using Marine Predators Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Flying Adhoc Network (FANET) has gained attention due to regressive real-time use of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). Optimized routing in FANETs is more challenging than mobile ad-hoc networks and vehicular ad-hoc networks due to restricted bandwidth and higher mobility of UAVs. Apart from the Mobile Adhoc Network (MANET) routing protocols, nature-inspired techniques-based optimized routing has shown promising routing performance in FANET. This paper proposes a Marine Predators Algorithm (MPA) based optimized routing protocol for FANET. The proposed routing technique selects a better routing path because of the high exploration and exploitation capabilities of MPA. The fitness function based on link stability and energy efficiency helps to select a routing path with better Quality of Service (QoS). The performance of the proposed technique has been analyzed based on packet arrival ratio, end-to-end delay, and throughput, and it is compared to five state-of-the-art techniques by varying the speed and number of the nodes. The simulation results depict that the proposed work is more efficient than the existing state-of-the-art schemes.

articleTitle: A Robust Security Method for Medical Image Based on 2D Schaffer Map
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: In this work, a methodology has been propounded for the security of the medical images containing Confusion and Diffusion phases in which a 2D Schaffer map is utilized. The confusion phase rearranges the row and column of medical images using the sorted indexes of the chaotic sequences produced by the Schaffer map. During the diffusion phase, the chaotic sequences are utilized to alter the pixel values of the original image through the XOR operation. This phase applies to both the row and column pixel values of the images, enhancing security. The efficacy of the proposed security method has been assessed through histogram analysis, chi-square, and variance test, revealing uniformity in encrypted image pixel values. The correlation analysis shows results closer to zero and an entropy value nearly equal to the ideal 8. Moreover, the encrypted image exhibits lower Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and higher Mean Square Error (MSE) values, indicating structural dissimilarity with the original image. The Unified Averaged Changed Intensity (UACI) value exceeds 33.40% and the Number of Changing Pixel Rate (NPCR) value exceeds 99.60%, indicating resistance against differential attacks, while the Structural Similarity Measure (SSIM) values closer to zero for the encrypted image indicates structural dissimilarity. The results affirm that the propounded methodology is secure from entropy, differential, statistical, and brute force attacks.

articleTitle: Direct Lightning Protection for PV Systems; A Novel Approach to Eliminate Shading Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Worldwide photovoltaic technologies are being deployed at an increasing rate due to the urgent effort to address climate change. The ability of the PV system to convert sunlight into electrical power at any size makes it very attractive to house owners, manufacturers, and commercial entities. To gain maximum output of the PV system, the panels must be installed at a location that is exposed to the sun without any shading. On a building, it is usually set up on the roof to avoid any possible shading during sunny hours. The desire to eliminate any shade, and expose the system to lightning strikes during storm conditions. The PV system is connected to the building or infrastructure electrical system. Therefore, under a lightning strike, the lightning energy can find its way to the building network causing severe damage, and could reach fatality. To reduce the risk of damage, engineers design direct and indirect lightning strikes. In this paper, the author addresses only the direct lightning protections. The work explains the role of the earth grid and the parameters that influence its performance. Also, the work proposed a novel layout of the lightning masts for a back-to-back east and west panel orientation where there is no room to extend the separation of PV rows. A case study is also included

articleTitle: An Application of Interpolation Search Algorithm to Curb the Impact of Outliers on the Dual-Axis Solar Tracking System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The world's need for energy is expanding quickly due to both the population boom and technological improvements. To meet future energy demands, it's crucial to choose a sustainable and cost-effective renewable energy source. Solar power is a crucial alternative to meet the ever growing global energy demand. Solar energy may be used to generate electricity either directly through photovoltaic (PV) cells or indirectly using concentrated solar power (CSP) technologies. As renewable energy technologies become more prevalent and have a significant influence on the global energy industry, it is imperative to continuously analyse their operational efficiency. The effectiveness of harvesting solar energy from a PV panel is impacted not only by changing climatic factors, but also by assembling angles, demand profile, latitude of the region of interest, and energy management system. The purpose of this paper is to present the empirical results of an impact of outliers on the dual-axis solar tracking system. An interpolation search algorithm is used to detect the outliers in the system by using the measured voltage from the PV panel. The algorithm observes the PV panel's immediate voltage and compares it with the previous voltage samples in order to establish if there is any drastic voltage difference that will translate to outliers. The algorithm was found to be incredibly precise and efficient for handling outliers in the solar tracking system. However, it still needs to be tested for the bigger PV arrays.

Author Keywords: dual-axis tracker and interpolation search algorithm

articleTitle: A Secured and Optimized Clustering Approch in Vehicular Ad-hoc Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) take vital role in intelligent transportation systems, but they face challenges due to dynamic network topology, impacting communication efficiency, especially with increasing active nodes. Security and privacy concerns are paramount, necessitating authentication to ensure only legitimate vehicles access the network. Secure vehicular clustering offers a solution, yet the number of clusters affects network dependability and efficiency. To tackle this, we present a secure clustering mechanism using Bat optimization algorithm, mimicking echolocation behavior to optimize clusters. We introduce an authentication technique for cluster heads to admit approved members, enhancing vehicular authentication. Simulations using MATLAB evaluate our approach, showing improved performance in end-to-end delay, overhead, and cluster head count compared to similar methods.

articleTitle: Effect of Link Breaks on Performance of MANETs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Mobile Ad Hoc Networks are known to be dynamic in nature and have no rigid or reliable network infrastructure by their very definition. They are expected to be self-governed and have dynamic wireless links which are not entirely reliable in terms of connectivity and security. Several factors could cause Link Breaks, such as mobility of nodes and / or their speeds of travel and attacks by malicious and selfish nodes which could result in packets being dropped which in turn could cause Link Breaks. This paper aims to study the effect of Link Breaks through two distinct causes i.e. Varying Node Speeds and Packet Drops by Malicious Nodes or due to any other reason on MANETs' performance only through Simulation, using Qualnet 7.4, the flagship product of Scalable Network Technologies and the commercialized version of GloMoSim, yet another popular product by the same manufacturers. We have done the simulation using AODV, the Ad hoc On-Demand Distance Vector Routing Protocol which is an industry standard among MANETs. AODV works on the common principles of Route Request, Route Reply and Route Error, the Route with the best metrics being chosen for message transmission. We have tried to compile the obtained results and analyze and justify the observed MANET behavior with reference to what could be predicted or expected.

articleTitle: Stretchable and Miniaturized Backscatter Antenna Based on Serpentine Metallic Structures and PDMS-BaTiO3 Composite
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: A miniaturized and stretchable backscatter antenna design used in backscatter communication is proposed. This structure concludes a stretchable substrate with customized high dielectric constant to achieve a miniaturized backscatter antenna. The stretchable substrate is fabricated by polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) and barium titanate (BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) powders with a special weight-ratio. In addition, the metallic structure of the antenna was converted into subwavelength-scale serpentine meshes. This approach reduces the physical size while achieving flexible and stretchable features of the antenna. With the RF switch and a backscatter circuit, the antenna realizes a binary phase shift keying (BPSK) modulation. This antenna is suitable for backscatter communication in wearable scenarios and has potential applications in future wearable devices.

articleTitle: Fabric-Based Absorber for Wearable RF Wireless Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: In this article, a fabric-based absorber for harvesting radio frequency (RF) wireless energy is proposed for wearable applications. The present absorber is comprised of periodic grooved bow-tie dipole arrays, fabric substrate and copper cloth ground. The copper cloth is utilized to produce periodic grooved bow-tie dipole arrays by laser cutting according to the pre-customized pattern. Then, the cutting-transfer method is utilized to transfer periodic copper cloth onto fabric substrate to integrate absorbing arrays consisting of 5 × 5 unit cells. Each unit cell comprises two pairs of grooved bow-tie dipoles. In addition, the unit cells of absorber are linked with a through channel to reduce power losses as well as transmit and gather the obtained energy from each column. Simulation results show that the proposed absorber can absorb more than 90% of the available energy at two resonant frequencies. Moreover, the rectifying circuit is set up and constantly improved, which could achieve the RF-dc efficiency of 56.6% and 40.4% at two resonant frequencies of the presented absorber. Finally, the fabric-based absorber integrated with rectifier circuit is fabricated and the measured dc voltage is 0.449V, which will hold promising applications for powering low-power wearable electronics.

articleTitle: Advanced Electrical Network Stability Using Hybrid PV & EV Systems in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This paper investigates the integration of electric vehicle (EV) and photovoltaic (PV) technologies into the power grid, with an emphasis on their significance for the advancement of sustainable energy. It mitigates the grid stability challenges posed by PV intermittentness and EV charging demands, encompassing voltage and frequency fluctuations. The research presents a set of effective management strategies and an all-encompassing mathematical model for evaluating different stabilization methods. It emphasizes the importance of smart inverters, demand response programs, and energy storage in augmenting the resilience and adaptability of the grid. This study describes how the deployment of hybrid PV and EV systems can substantially increase the system's efficiency while maintaining a high level of network stability, thereby contributing to sustainable energy objectives. An included case study captures both scenarios, system stability with the presence of the grid and with the support of a diesel generator.

articleTitle: Antenna Delay Calibration in an IR-UWB Radar Simulated by Vector Network Analyzer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This work presents a novel method for antenna delay calibration in an Impulse Radio Ultra-WideBand (IR-UWB) radar system, utilizing a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) for simulation. The calibration approach involves adjusting the distance between a metallic plate and the radar device to compute the echo signal's flight time at various distances. The system delay is determined by measuring the S21 parameter and applying differential noise reduction techniques, enabling accurate localization of the echo signal's emission point. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves the accuracy of distance measurements, with errors maintained within millimeter tolerances.

articleTitle: Phase Current Reconstruction of Switched Reluctance Motor from Inverter Current Based on Pulse Injection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Current sampling is an important part of switched reluctance motor (SRM) control system, but the current sensor in the drive system will increase the drive volume and cost. To diminish the count of current sensors and enhance driver reliability, this paper introduces a phase current reconstruction method derived from inverter current modulation through pulse injection. High frequency pulse is injected into the conduction phase, and the inverter current is analyzed according to the control mode and the state of the conduction phase, and the phase current is reconstructed. The proposed approach solely employs a current sensor on the inverter bus, obviating the necessity for circuit structure alteration, and can realize the current reconstruction of current chopper control (CCC) and voltage chopper control (CVC) under soft chopper and hard chopper conditions. The proposed scheme is verified to be feasible on 800W 12/8 SRM platform.

articleTitle: Tech in Social Control: Analyzing the Impact of Technology on Monitoring and Shaping Social Behavior of Filipinos
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Influences, ethical dilemmas, and the integration of artificial intelligence, the research provides valuable insights. Survey findings reflect public awareness and perceptions, revealing a delicate balance between societal benefits and individual privacy. The study contributes to discussions on responsible technology development, emphasizing transparency and ongoing scrutiny to navigate the ethical implications of monitoring technologies in today's rapidly changing world.

articleTitle: Superimposed Root Locus Portraits for Parametric Synthesis of Robust Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Mechatronic devices and equipment, such as electric drives, cutting tools, robots, etc., often operate in conditions of uncertainty, which leads to the lack of their control systems robustness and thus to degradation of their dynamic characteristics. The paper represents a method for robust automatic control system parametric synthesis, considering that two physical parameters are variable (uncertain)s. Mathematical model of the dynamic system is defined in the form of the root locus portrait (root locus) with two physical parameters variation within infinite intervals of their real values (interval parametric uncertainty). A notion of the system “superimposed root locus” (“superimposed root locus portrait”) has been introduced, which is used for calculation of the parameters' values ensuring the dynamic system robust stability. Two different approaches are proposed for the task solution: the first one relies on the extended free root locus application and the second one - on the regular root loci application. Graphical root locus portraits are considered to illustrate the system response to plant parameters' variation.

articleTitle: Evaluating Modern Information Extraction Techniques for Complex Document Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The exponential increase in digital data has necessitated the development of advanced models for Key Information Extraction (KIE) from text-heavy documents. Traditional Optical Character Recognition (OCR) systems have evolved to incorporate multimodal vision approaches, enhancing their capacity to extract not just text but also tables, key-value pairs, figures, and other significant document components. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the state-of-the-art models including Visual Information Extraction, Semantic Entity Recognition (SER), Relation Extraction (RE), and Document Layout Analysis. Despite considerable advancements, these methods still encounter various challenges that undermine their effectiveness and efficiency. This paper presents a comparative study of five different information extraction approaches applied to a carefully curated dataset of text-heavy documents, including various types such as forms, invoices, and long-form legal and medical reports. Our findings demonstrate that this integrated OCR and multimodal vision approach achieves superior accuracy compared to other approaches. We present a critical analysis of the challenges faced in this domain and propose suggestions for future research to refine information extraction capabilities.

articleTitle: Financial Time Series Prediction on Apple Stocks Using Machine and Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The scope of financial time series prediction has evolved significantly, driven by the surging availability of data and computational advancements. This transition has seen the traditional statistical methods give way to present-day machine learning and deep learning techniques. Despite these strides, challenges continue to exist, with market unpredictability, dimensionality issues, and overfitting in high-frequency data standing as primary obstacles. Newer machine learning models are better than old ones at predicting stocks. When electronic trading and yield optimisation come together, they make these models even better. Deep learning has completely changed machine learning, especially in forecasting financial trends over time. Complex deep learning models lack interpretability, hindering real-world adoption. Considering this we have used two deep learning models which are Long Short-Term Memory and Convolutional Neural Network and trained these on apple stock market data over the years along with one machine learning model i.e. Linear Regression. Then we have compared the accuracy of all the models based on their R-squared Score value.

articleTitle: Leveraging Vehicle Predictive Analytics through Adaptive Learning and Cloud-Aided Sensor Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This study presents an innovative framework that integrates adaptive learning and cloud-based sensor fusion in order to improve the prediction of vehicle dynamics using passive data from vehicular sensors. The methodology aims to improve autonomous vehicles by harnessing relevant Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS) features using real-time data from a network of vehicles to continuously improve predictive models. This system enhances the interpretation of data from many sources by combining sensor fusion and machine learning. By adapting to new information, it achieves precise real-time predictions. An optimization approach is introduced to streamline the implementation of cloud-based systems and minimize computational requirements. The effectiveness and adaptability of the framework surpasses those of conventional models, as demonstrated by empirical evidence. This highlights the capacity of the paradigm to radically revolutionize vehicle automation by allowing for more accurate prediction of vehicle dynamics. This study signifies an advancement in the enhancement of transportation that is both safer and more effective by utilizing collective data from vehicles to continuously improve and acquire knowledge.

articleTitle: Developing A Design of Single Axis Sun-Sensor Solar Tracking System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This paper proposes a new technique for a single-direction solar tracker. The propped design is based on a sun sensor system that controls the position of the solar panel. The sun sensors of the proposed design contain four photodiodes that are placed on the solar panel with specific angles and directions. The proposed system shows several advantages such as the simplicity of implementing the system. This system is based on the real-time tracking of sunlight with low cost of applying a single direction tracker. A Simulink MATLAB is applied to show the advantages of applying a single-direction tracker by following the angle of sunlight during the day. The data of real-time, sun position, and irradiation of the sun are applied to the simulation.

articleTitle: Recession From Declination of Economic Activities Dictated by Conditional Probabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: From a probabilistic model, this paper demonstrates that recession might be in essence the main event constituted by the conjunction of financial crisis, adverse supply shock, natural causes, serious declination of gross domestic product, among others factors, all of them entangled each other but dictated by the theorem of Bayes. Thus, this paper proposes the idea that recession from the mathematical point of view is the fall of spending as consequence of convoluted probabilistic distribution function through kernel functions that might be mathematically interpreted as the recoil on (i) production, (ii) consumption, (iii) investment, and (iv) employment. In this manner, recession might be understood as the Bayesian scenario by which variables are conditioned each other.

articleTitle: A Vertical-Structured LED with Improved Current Distribution Uniformity and Illumination Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: A new vertical LED structure was proposed recently to solve the uneven current spreading density problem of traditional Y-shaped vertical structure LED. In this paper, we investigated the current density and near-field light intensity distribution of the proposed vertical structured LED at different wavelengths and compared with typical designs. Five wavelengths were chosen for comparison: deep ultraviolet light, ultraviolet light, violet light, blue light, and green light. We found that the current distributions were distinct for different wavelengths, therefore different layout should be employed to optimize the efficiency at specific wavelength. The new structure exhibited superior current spreading and light emitting uniformity at all wavelengths. The WPEs were also greatly improved in the proposed structures. The suggested layout for specific configurations will be presented.

articleTitle: Fiber Bragg Grating Temperature Sensor Evaluation from Simulation to Practical Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This work proposes studying the sensors with Bragg gratings and analyzing temperature sensors based on this principle. The project theme fits into current trends in the field of sensors, which should provide good integrability, fast response, high sensitivity, and accuracy-implementing such a sensor that uses Bragg grating in the single-mode silica fiber. We aim to give the central wavelength of 1550 nm at 25 degrees Celsius. The function of temperature variation on the gratings the central wavelength of signal response changes the value as follows: for the temperature under 25 Celsius degrees, the central wavelength of reflection signal shifts left, and for the temperature above 25 Celsius degrees, the central wavelength shifts right. The reference is 1550 nm.

articleTitle: Modeling of 100W-18V Solar Panel Using MATLAB/Simulink and Proteus Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This study describes the modeling and simulation of photovoltaic (PV) for a 100W-18V solar panel prototype using Matlab/Simulink and Proteus. Using the manufacturer's data sheet as a reference, we compare and evaluate our findings with the nonlinear characteristics of current versus voltage (I-V) and power vs voltage (P-V). Finally, we apply all of the values from Matlab/Simulink to the Proteus simulator. The model used by Proteus is based on the single-diode, which depicts the appropriate circuit of a solar panel. Proteus software has been used to run simulations to evaluate the effectiveness of the solar under various environmental circumstances, standard test settings, and abrupt shifts in the solar irradiance as well as the temperature can be used. In this work, the shading and series/parallel resistances have all been considered. PV array has been simulated in Proteus to improve model simulation. This work might also serve as a guide for less experienced researchers studying PV panels on how to replicate a PV in various ways.

articleTitle: Electrical Modeling of Near-Field Coupling Inside Integrated Heterogeneous Packages
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This paper presents prediction models for capacitive and inductive coupling between passive and active packaged components. The model uses mutual inductance and capacitance between a source and a receptor to predict voltage noise due to mutual parasitics with simple circuit models. These parasitic parameters are estimated from Q3D Ansys and analytical equations. Full-wave electromagnetic simulations are used to validate the accuracy of the circuit models with the estimated parasitics. Lateral and vertical coupling scenarios are studied. Near-field coupling between two transmission lines is considered to represent lateral capacitive coupling between two RF interconnects. The near-field transmission coupling based on the analytical model was −18.5 dB. However, according to 3D EM models, the coupling varies from −16 to −17.5 dB. Secondly, the model is extended and used to predict inductive coupling between a Hartly oscillator and power amplifier (P A) chips that are vertically integrated in a 3D package. The noise voltage based on the inductive coupling is 50–500 11 V, corresponding to an isolation of −85 to −65 dB, across 2–4 GHz for mutual inductances varying from 4 to 21 pH. Circuit models with Q3D estimates of parasitics are shown to replicate full-wave electromagnetic simulations with good accuracy. The model effectively estimates near-field coupling between components without needing the near-field scanning data, by solely relying on package geometry.

articleTitle: Dense Image Registration Using Global Optical Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Accurate and dense motion tracking is a crucial necessity for numerous video feature extraction algorithms. This paper develops a technique for calculating camera trajectories in a 3D global coordinate system assuming its swift motion. The proposed algorithm is based on a disparity rather than image depth approach. Moreover, a Laplacian pyramid and dense optical flow methods are used. Highly accurate matching of two consecutive keyframes is essential for reconstructing 3D scenes as it facilitates the retrieval of the three-dimensional geometry of the scene from captured images. Numerical tests are provided and confirm the robustness and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Maximizing Energy Yield: The Optimal Tilt Angle and Orientation in Agrivoltaic Systems with Light Productivity Factor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The combined agriculture and photovoltaic system are a trade-off between the amount of light received by the solar panel and the percentage of the light reaching the ground level. The light reduction percentage (% LR) factor for a specific plant, cultivated under the agrivoltaic (AV) system has been taken into consideration by previous research. Previous research considered the Light Reduction Percentage (% LR) factor for a specific plant in the agrivoltaic (AV) system, indicating a 40.92 % light reduction under a fixed structure, meeting Photo-synthetically Active Radiation (PAR) requirements. This study introduces the Light Productivity Factor (LPF) [1] along with light reduction to maximize energy yield, determine structural requirements, and supervise harvesting conditions for the crops. The main purpose is to estimate optimal tilt angles and orientations for fixed-tilted Photovoltaic (PV) structures, optimizing irradiance collection on PV modules while meeting minimum light reduction for shade-tolerant plants. Results demonstrate satisfactory agrivoltaic system performance with a maximum total irradiance of 1929 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kW / m ^2 / year$</tex>, light reduction of 36.73 % for monofacial and 39.06 % for bifacial module, and LPF values of 0.9 and 1.5 for monofacial and bifacial panels respectively and determining the value of tilt angle of 9° for both the panel type and orientation of 190° for monofacial and 185° for bifacial module respectively.

articleTitle: Theory of Diffusive Dynamics of Bacteria Population from Probabilistic Interactions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: As seen in some bacteria populations their chemotactic motility would depend on all those events that involves physics as well as biochemical interactions that are favorable to them in order to exert the best space-time strategies to conquer any type of environment. Thus, in this paper the colonization of a substrate is perceived as stochastic event so that it is possible to apply probabilistic formulations such as the well-known Bayes theorem. It is demonstrated that a probabilistic chemotaxis would be related to the diffusion equation, fact that would support the idea that bacteria might exhibit a diffusive but also random behavior. Simulations are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Sustainable Smart Road: A Unified Cost Estimation Model for Renewable-Powered Smart Roads
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: With new stringent policies affecting the transport and generation sectors, new technologies have emerged to drive the electric and technological transition. One of these is the smart road, a highly sensorised system to enable the integration of new vehicles and safety technologies. In this paper, the implementation of a smart road is simulated, first from an energy point of view and then from an economic point of view, by identifying the power demand of components and their cost. Next, the energetic core of the smart road is implemented. The energy core consists of a PV plant capable of powering the infrastructure. In this paper a simulation to test the proposed methodology is implemented. In the case study, a 280.05 kW smart road is powered by an optimally dimensioned PV plant. The production guaranteed by the 283.8 kWp plant will be 389.49 MW <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex>/year and requires <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5723\mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex>. Furthermore, the 234.57 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{k}\unicode{x20AC}$</tex> investment for the plant will represent less than 10% of the total investment, highlighting how renewable integration can be an economic sustainable purpose. Finally, another method to return the investment as quickly as possible will be proposed.

articleTitle: A Research on a 3.5kW Class Inverter Applying Multi-Level Switching Technology to Improve Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: A circuit that can implement a multi-level inverter using one capacitor instead of the three capacitors used in the conventional flying capacitor clamped multi-level inverter which increases the switching states and circuit's complexity is proposed in this paper. By replacing three flying capacitors with one flying capacitor, the number of switching cells and the ratings of each component such as MOSFET and filter can be reduced. Therefore, a high-capacity inverter can be designed with small-capacity elements, and an output close to a sinewave can be created, which is also advantageous in improving power conversion efficiency and power factor. In addition, since the switching voltages can be reduced, the frequency fluctuation rate and total harmonic distortion (THD) rate can be improved. In order words, to analyze the performance characteristics and power quality of the proposed circuit, a 3.5kW class inverter was designed and the experiments were conducted to confirm its performance such as efficiency, power factor, frequency fluctuation and THD. Through the experiment, the results were confirmed that the maximum power conversion efficiency of 98.01 %, the power factor of 0.99, the THD rate of below about 3%, and the output frequency fluctuation rate of 0.01 % were confirmed over the entire load range of the proposed circuit.

articleTitle: An Optimised QPSO-Based Algorithm for Power Management in Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: As we gradually modernize and turn legacy power grid systems into their smart equivalents, called Smart Grids (SGs), they must still be optimized in terms of both energy generation and its management. Smart grids employ various optimization methods to conserve energy, lower expenses, and tackle security concerns in energy generation, transmission, and distribution across different domains. The paper focuses on the optimization methods applicable to energy management in SGs. Thus, we propose and explore an approach to solving the day-ahead dispatch model in such systems (SGs) with distributed generation (DG). The approach addresses the non-linear cost function and proposes a framework to handle the “valve-point” loading effect of DGs. It further evaluates the impact of Demand-Side Management (DSM) on energy management systems and examines load dynamics within the SG over fifteen-minute scheduling intervals. The study relies on the Quantum Particle Swarm Optimization (QPSO) algorithm to tackle the non-linear DGs cost optimization problem, leading to a 5% reduction in OPEX costs with minimal impact on customer satisfaction or utility.

articleTitle: A Study on Enhanced Generation Algorithm Through Structure-Preserving Style Transfer with SLIC
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to consider the structure of images in the Style Transfer model proposed in “Perceptual Losses for Real-time Super Resolution and Style Transfer”. This paper addresses the optimization problem outlined in “Image Style Transfer Using Convolutional Neural Networks” using feed-forward networks. While conducting style transfer by distinguishing between content and style, the existing method does not take into account the structure of images. Considering the structure of the original image enables better image generation. To achieve this, we employ techniques inspired by the structure representation in “Learning to Cartoonize Using White-box Cartoon Representations”. We utilize SLIC segmentation for superpixels and represent the structure through adaptive coloring. The structured image is included in the loss function for computation. The results of this paper confirm the generation of images that better capture small details such as faces compared to existing methods. The proposed method is expected to further advance through future integration with instance segmentation and other optimization techniques.

articleTitle: Novel CMOS Circuit for Fuzzification: Implementing a Sigmoid Activation Function in Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This paper introduces a novel circuit design based on current-mode principles, tailored for the hardware implementation of a programmable analog Membership Function Circuit (MFC) Sigmoid function. It is simple CMOS compatible, operates on voltage signals, and delivers an output current corresponding to the desired activation function. By adjusting the reference voltage, the inflection point in the sigmoid function can be conveniently modified. This structure is also general purpose in tuning the slope of Membership Functions (MFs) using scaled transistors with different <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{W}{L}$</tex> ratios. Simulation of the proposed circuit in the LTspice software using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$45nm$</tex> CMOS technology, with level 54 parameters, indicates low power dissipation, measuring at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$12\mu W$</tex> with a supply voltage of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 1.1V$</tex>. This proposal represents a significant advancement for potential applications in neural networks.

articleTitle: Influence of heat transfer fluid on the thermodynamic performance of PCM-based thermal management system in fuel cell vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Fuel cell-based electric vehicles (FCEV) are gaining recognition owing to their no emissions technology, non-dependence on fossil fuels, low-temperature operation and reliability. However, for commercialization, the thermal management system (TMS) in existing FCEVs needs improvement as its oversized radiators needlessly augment the weight and volume of the vehicle. The study presents an energetic and exergetic evaluation of the recently proposed phase change material (PCM) based TMS, with different heat transfer fluids (HTFs - H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O, (CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>OH)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>+H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O, and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>OH) to identify the most suitable HTF for commercial use. The highest energy and exergy efficiencies reported for H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O are 61.96% and 72.95%, for (CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>OH)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>+H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O are 61.72% and 69.67%, and for C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>OH are 60.97% and 65.72%, respectively. Additionally, the study investigates the effect of mass flow rate (2.95 kg/s to 5.04 kg/s) and specific heat capacity (2.46 to 4.20 kJ/kg°C) of the HTFs on the system performance. The results indicate that the specific heat capacity of the HTF has more influence on the system than its mass flow rate. The influence of specific heat capacity on the exergetic efficiency is ~7.25% more than the influence of mass flow rate.

articleTitle: A Security Algorithm to Prevent Denial of Service Attacks in the Internet of Things Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has emerged as a pervasive network of interconnected devices embedded with sensors and electronics, enabling data collection and communication. However, the burgeoning number of internet-connected devices within the IoT ecosystem presents significant challenges in safeguarding consumer privacy and security. This growing attack surface exposes vulnerabilities that malicious actors can exploit. Denial of Service (DoS) and Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks are prominent threats within the IoT landscape. In a DoS attack, attackers overwhelm a device or network with a flood of illegitimate requests, hindering legitimate users from accessing services. A DDoS attack amplifies this disruption by leveraging numerous compromised systems to launch a coordinated assault. The dynamic nature of DoS attacks, coupled with the inherent complexities of the IoT environment, often render existing security solutions ineffective, allowing attackers to circumvent them. This paper proposes a novel approach to address these challenges. We present a mathematical model for DoS attack detection within the IoT, leveraging queuing theory principles. This model forms the foundation for a multi-hierarchical firewall architecture designed to safeguard IoT devices. The firewall incorporates a distributed service architecture to enhance its ability to handle concurrent requests. The performance evaluation of this proposed solution will be conducted through simulations, with results presented in a forthcoming study.

articleTitle: AccessFlex: Flexible Attribute Based Access Control Scheme for Sharing Access Privileges in Cloud Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: With the rapid growth of cloud storage adoption, ensuring efficient access control and tamper verification has become a critical concern. This paper presents AccessFlex, a Flexible Attribute-Based Access Control Scheme for Sharing Access Privileges in Cloud Storage. The proposed system is developed using Python and MySQL database servers to achieve robust and secure cloud storage management. AccessFlex introduces three key actors in the system: Admin, Data Owner, and Data User. Admin manages cryptography keys and data consumer attributes. Data Owners can securely upload files to the cloud storage server and define access details for Data Users. Data Users are granted access to authorized files based on their attributes. The AccessFlex system guarantees confidentiality, integrity, and accountability, providing a comprehensive solution for secure file management in cloud storage environments. By leveraging attribute-based access control, masking, and encryption techniques, the system offers flexibility and scalability, catering to diverse access requirements while safeguarding sensitive data from unauthorized access and modifications. For data security existing RSA encryption techniques are used.

articleTitle: Generative Adversarial Networks for Augmentation of Simulation Scenarios in Ground Penetrating Radar Based Demining
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Ground-penetrating radar (GPR) has proven effective in search of buried landmines or improvised explosive devices (IEDs).
