However, the interpretation of such GPR data by a human operator is inefficient. Automating this task may provide a remedy. For this purpose, methods from supervised machine learning (ML) show great promise, though generally requiring vast amounts of labeled training data. Fortunately, computer simulations enable safe and feasible data acquistion. In this regard, we have previously proposed a fast but still accurate two-dimensional simulation concept based on the finite-difference frequency-domain technique, which is able to account for a wide range of scenarios. The objective of this contribution is to further augment the diversity of these scenarios and, consequently, of the corresponding training data. To this end, we integrate methods from data augmentation (DA), namely generative adversarial networks (GANs). As qualitatively evaluated, a variety of scenarios in a quick and simple, yet realistic manner can be created thereby.

articleTitle: Precision Oncology: Deciphering Drug Sensitivity Through Multi-Omics Clustering and Machine Learning in Cancer Cell Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This study combines diverse omics datasets, including Proteomic, Transcriptomic, Genomic, Metabolomic and miRNA profiles from cancer cell lines, with Drug Sensitivity (AUC) data for 285 drugs. We used the k-means clustering algorithm to group cell lines based on multi-omics data. Drug sensitivity (AUC) for 285 drugs were predicted using Random Forest Classifier. The resulting 5 clusters were thoroughly evaluated, suggesting drugs with over 75% accuracy for further scrutiny. Our findings indicate that the cluster-specific approach consistently outperforms the non-clustering approach. Notably, the maj ority of clusters exhibit a higher number of drugs with over 75% accuracy compared to the non-clustered approach. Moreover, the mean accuracy for identified drugs is greater for most clusters than the non-clustering approach. However, while there are some common drugs across clusters, each cluster predominantly shows a unique set of drugs. This emphasizes the importance of tailoring therapeutic strategies to the diverse molecular profiles identified within each cluster. This refined approach enhances our understanding of drug responses, supporting a cluster-centric strategy in precision oncology. It highlights the importance of customizing treatments based on the diverse molecular landscapes of cancer cell lines, contributing to the advancement of personalized treatment strategies.

articleTitle: Mechanical, Dielectric, and Thermal Stability Characterization of Spark Plasma Sintered $\text{TiO}_{2}$ PI Nanocomposites for Energy-Power Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Polyimide (PI) is a high performance polymer characterized with unique properties including mechanical strength to weight ratio, flexibility, excellent breakdown strength, good thermal stability, and easy processability. However, the low dielectric constant and mechanical degradation of PI remains a challenge facing its energy storage density performance. Thus, this study investigated the impact of titania <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{TiO}_{2})$</tex> nano-fillers on the mechanical, dielectric, and thermal stability of PI-based nanocomposite material for advanced energy-power applications using spark plasma sintering technology. The microstructure, mechanical, dielectric, and thermal stability of the sintered material was evaluated using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), nano-indenter, inductance (L) capacitance (C) resistance (R) meter, and thermogravimetric analyzer (TGA), respectively. The SEM result shows uniform dispersion of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TiO}_{2}$</tex> nanoparticles into the PI matrix. The hardness and elastic modulus of the PI matrix was enhanced by 24.9% and 10%, respectively, at 4 wt% <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TiO}_{2}$</tex> addition. The nanocomposites depicted improved dielectric constant, low dielectric loss, low electrical conductivity, high dielectric strength, and larger energy density of about 8.4%, 86.1%, 86.1%, 7.1%, and 24.5% at 50 kHz in comparison to the virgin PI. In addition, the thermal stability and heat-resistance index of the PI matrix was enhanced by introducing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TiO}_{2}$</tex> nanofillers. The findings suggest the facile technique to produce <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TiO}_{2}/\text{PI}$</tex>-based nanocomposites with characteristics required for advanced energy and power related applications.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Intrusion Detection for Cybersecurity in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: In this article, we have proposed Deep Learning techniques for cybersecurity in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). UAVs, also known as drones, have become versatile tools used in many applications. However, UA V cybersecurity remains a major concern due to the evolution of cyberattacks. Faced with this issue, it is important to give a contribution on intrusion detection systems (IDS) to be applied in UAVs, given that existing cybersecurity solutions still present limitations. It is in this context that we have proposed Deep Learning-based intrusion detection models such as Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and the combination of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models (CNN+LSTM) and these are evaluated using the CICIDS2017 dataset. Based on their performance, the proposed models are compared with Machine Learning models to decide on the best model for intrusion detection in UAVs. Thus, the results obtained during the experiment indicate that the hybrid CNN-LSTM model obtained a high accuracy of 99.063% compared to the other models.

articleTitle: Double Decay Parameter Estimation with Autoregressive and Differential Linear Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Presented in this paper is a method of formulating a double-decay nuclear process parameter estimation problem as a linear regression problem that can be analytically solved. The resulting linear regression problem is solved for data simulated with electrical circuits and a computer model. In the first scenario, with computer-generated data, the linear regression problem leads to an accurate estimation for double-decay process parameters. In the second scenario with circuit-based simulated data, the linear regression solution yields a reasonable solution but it is significantly shifted by the process and measurement noise from the circuit and measuring devices.

articleTitle: DViTPolyp: Small Polyp Detection in Colonoscopy Videos based on Deep Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Early detection of colorectal polyps and removal play a crucial role in the prevention of colon cancer. Computer-aided detection (CAD) methods can be employed to help endoscopists reduce the polyp miss-rates. Numerous automatic polyp detection methods have been explored. However, it is still challenging to automatically detect colon polyps in small size in colonoscopy videos. This paper presents a method termed DViTPolyp for detecting small colorectal polyp in colonoscopy videos. The proposed method leverages the power of the deep vision transformer as the detection head in the network to aggregate rich global features, and uses the re-attention mechanism to regenerate attention maps to capture the features from the backbone model and DViT block. Also, we propose to use a power regularized Intersection Over Union (IoU) as the loss function to further enhance the accuracy of detection. Experiments are conducted on a mix of several public polyp datasets. Comparative results show that our proposed method has a better performance than other methods.

articleTitle: Critical Factors Influencing Impulsive Buying in Live Streaming E-Commerce Environments: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: In the era of technological evolution, Live Streaming, as a business model, has revolutionized e-commerce, enabling streamers, vendors, and influencers to showcase and sell products in real-time to a vast global online audience, transforming the shopping experience. This study focused on the primary research question: “What are the critical factors that lead to impulsive buying actions in Live Streaming E-Commerce?” Understanding these factors is crucial for businesses aiming to optimize their Live Streaming E-Commerce strategies. By following their approach to align with the identified variables, organizations can enhance customer engagement, product appeal, and the overall shopping environment. Adopting a Systematic Literature Review methodology, insights from diverse authors and sources were collected to seek the factors influencing impulsive buying during live streaming commerce. The focus spanned studies published between 2019 and 2023. The comprehensive literature review revealed 46 factors across 41 scholarly articles, categorized into five latent variables: User Experience & Engagement, Environment & External, Product, User Behavioral & Psychological, and Streamer. Our findings not only offer valuable insights for organizations in the Live Streaming E-Commerce sphere but also present an opportunity for businesses to strategically stimulate impulsive buying behavior. As live streaming commerce continues to evolve, further research is necessary to deeply dive into how these identified factors influence impulsive buying behaviors in a specific Live Streaming E-Commerce context. Additional studies examining the significance and interplay of these factors would provide more precise insights into the most relevant stimuli triggering impulsive purchases.

articleTitle: A Comparative Performance Analysis of Task Scheduling Algorithms in Federated Clouds
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Efficient task scheduling is crucial in the domain of cloud computing. Cloud computing is a service that allows users to access and share virtual resources as needed in order to fulfil their jobs. The primary objective of task scheduling is to execute tasks in a manner that maximizes performance by fully utilizing resources and minimising losses. Several scheduling algorithms currently exist with the goal of achieving various objectives, including minimising execution time, cost, makespan, enhancing resource utilisation, and load balancing. This study evaluates and compares the performance of six scheduling algorithms, including Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO), Ant Colony Optimisation (ACO), Q-Learning, Round Robin (RR), First-Come, First-Served (FCFS), and Shortest Job First (SJF) algorithms. The algorithms' performance is assessed by comparing them using standard measures, such as makespan, execution time, and throughput, across various workload scenarios through graphical representation of the findings. The study employs Java and CloudSim for the purpose of implementing and evaluating. The Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO) algorithm exhibits exceptional efficiency, particularly in minimising makespan, obtaining optimal throughput, and attaining the shortest execution time. The capacity to adjust to changing settings and efficiently utilise resources continually demonstrates its worth in many situations. The study emphasizes the pivotal significance of algorithm selection and data centre layout in optimising work scheduling, particularly in dynamic and distributed cloud computing systems.

articleTitle: Relationship of Energy Use, CO2 Emissions and Economic Growth in Rwanda
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Even though the contribution of Rwanda's carbon dioxide (CO2) is little at global level, it brings dramatic problems, and affect several sectors including the agriculture sector which the majority of the population relies on. Energy consumption and Economic growth can be obviously on the list of drivers of pollution. The aims of the study is to highlight the drivers of CO2 emissions in Rwanda. This study tries to investigate the relationship between Energy use, Carbon dioxide emissions, and Economic growth with Rwanda as a case study by employing a time series data that span from 1990 to 2020, the simulation was performed using Low Emissions Analysis Platform (LEAP) software. The obtained results shows that the carbon emission in Rwanda is affected by the energy consumption. And also the energy consumption increase as the economic growth increases. This was justified by the increase of electricity access rate in rural area and urban area. Also as the GDP increase, citizens tend to improve their living standards by increasing home appliances which results in additional energy consumption. But on the other hand we have seen than the increase in LPG gas for cooking has reduced the use of charcoal in urban area. Therefore there is a relationship between energy consumption, GDP and carbon emission in Rwanda.

articleTitle: Analysis of Physical Layer Impairments Resources Allocation Aware Algorithm/Framework in Transparent OTNs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Present-day, limitedly fixed wavelength routed based all Transparent Optical Transport Networks (OTNs) are quite energy efficient in comparison to translucent and opaque equivalents. As a result they are also regarded as a practical solution transport network provisioning ultrahigh bandwidth capabilities to support the various applications and services. The resulting heterogeneous nature of present-day global traffic makes such wavelength-routed networks spectrally inefficient. However, advancements in DSP techniques, modulation approaches, and transmission impairment mitigation techniques have vastly improved such net-works' spectral efficiencies and optical reach. The paper thus reviews the efficiency in the operation of an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) based Transparent OTN that is characterized by flexibility in the provisioning of available spectral resources. We address the challenges of optimal routing level allocation of wavelengths subject to maximizing spectral efficiencies. In so doing, we also consider the impact of various physical impairments. We introduce a quality factor-based tool (Q-factor) that aids in choosing op-timal routes. Ultimately, The tool is later incorporated into a proposed resource allocation framework's algorithms, which focus on ensuring spectral efficiency and overall network energy-efficient operation. Overall, we conclude that the pro-posed transport network architecture is relatively efficient regarding energy and spectral efficiencies.

articleTitle: The Potential of Exhaust Waste Heat Recovery (WHR) from a Diesel-Gen-Set via Rankine Cycle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Approximately one-third of fuel energy in internal combustion engines dissipates as exhaust gas heat, posing a significant obstacle to electricity generation. Interest in recovering this waste heat is growing, and this paper proposes a solution by utilizing surplus heat from a diesel engine to enhance power generation through a Waste Heat Recovery (WHR) system. The main objectives are to improve power generation efficiency by simulating and optimizing the WHR system using Engineering Equation Solver (EES), focusing on maximizing power output and freshwater production while minimizing costs. For a 1.1 MW diesel-gen-set, the system achieves a remarkable net additional power production of 131.0 kW, with an expected payback period of 4.8 years. Additionally, the WHR system can produce 8.56 ML/year of freshwater with a payback period of 4.63 years. Combining additional power and freshwater production reduces the payback period to just 2.0 years. Key parameters such as maintaining a 100 kPa absolute exhaust pressure, an aspect ratio of approximately 3, and a pinch temperature of 20 K provide valuable operational insights. Sensitivity analysis of these parameters enhances understanding of their impact on system performance, guiding future research toward more efficient and sustainable WHR systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing Container Security with Per-Process Per-Container Egress Packet Filtering Using eBPF
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: With growing use of containers and container or-chestration in production systems, it is more important than ever to secure compromised containers from malicious uses. A compromised container could become a part of a botnet or could talk back to an attacker's server, exposing sensitive information. In this paper, we discuss the implementation of a packet filter which filters packets based on their L3 and L4 headers as well as their process and container of origin. To achieve this, we use extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) programs to probe into kernel functions and use hook points provided by the kernel to monitor and filter egress packets. Primarily, we use an eBPF program of type 'BPF _PROG_TYPE_CGROUP _SKB’ that not only allows us to filter TCPIUDP packets, but also packets transmitted over raw sockets (e.g, ICMP packets). To attach this program to any new containers, we also explore an in-kernel solution to detect new containers at runtime. We conclude the paper by conducting an experiment to measure the latency overhead added by our proposed solution.

articleTitle: GAN-Based Defense Mechanism Against Word-Level Attacks for Arabic Transformer-Based Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Recent studies have revealed that deep learning models are vulnerable to adversarial examples, which are small perturbations that are added to the input to fool the model. However, many researchers are proposing new strategies to defend the models that were trained on English corpora. In this paper, we focus on Transformer-based models for low-resource languages like Arabic, which encounter numerous challenges, including word-substitution attacks. These attacks can produce inaccurate and unreliable results and represent a type of adversarial example. To address this, we propose a defense mechanism based on Generative Adversarial Networks (i.e., InfoGANs) that can effectively protect Transformer-based models for Arabic language from word-substitution attacks. Our approach involves applying GAN strategy as defense mechanism by extracting the text embedding vectors from our Transformer-based model (Arabert) and injected them to the generator in the training phase to produce perturbed examples that are difficult to distinguish from the original data, while the discriminator in GAN is tasked with correctly identifying the genuine examples. The proposed method has shown promising results in defending Transformer-based models against word-substitution attacks on the Arabic language. As a result, we find that the accuracy recovered from various types of attacks that we employed on our two datasets ranged from 2% to 20%.

articleTitle: A Novel Nonlinear Averaged Model for a Flyback Converter with Peak Current Mode Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a novel nonlinear averaged model to be used in the analysis of systems with multiple components that include a flyback converter operated under peak current mode control (PCMC). Most traditional approaches often use linear models that are not suitable for capturing the transient behavior needed in applications with time scales several orders of magnitude above the switching frequency. We address these limitations by incorporating the dynamic behavior using a nonlinear model that significantly improves the accuracy of existing linear models while being general enough to be used with standard numerical integration methods. In addition to the detailed analytical derivation, both simulation and experimental validation demonstrate the efficacy of our model in a study case with an RC parallel load. The application presented promises to offer considerable benefits in terms of computational efficiency for dynamic analysis in a wide range of applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Interlink Converter Reliability in Energy-Constrained Optimal Energy Management System of Hybrid AC/DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Interlink Converter (ILC) is the backbone of the hybrid AC/DC microgrid (HMG), and any failure in its operation may lead to financial and technical losses. The reliability enhancement of the ILC is paramount, as it is responsible for power exchange between sub-grids to maintain system stability and facilitate optimal energy transactions in economic scheduling. Besides, battery energy storage system (BESS) play a pivotal role in coping with the intermittent behaviour of renewable energy sources and the economic operation of grid-connected HMGs by charging at low energy prices and discharging to the grid at high energy prices. Given that BESS represent one of the most expensive components in electricity networks, it is imperative to account for their capacity fading constraints in the optimal energy management system. This paper introduces a reliability index for the ILC based on the Arrhenius equation, while also exploring the energy throughput constraint to mitigate the cyclic aging of the BESS. Through three comprehensive case studies, the simulation results signify the remarkable effectiveness of the proposed energy management system in reducing the failure rate of the ILC and mitigating the cyclic aging of the BESS.

articleTitle: Analysis and Solutions to Reconstruction Errors Caused by Different Aspect Ratios in Structured Light System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Structured light system can be used to reconstruct the 3D profile of the object by encoding projected patterns and decoding the captured images. Generally, there are several different types of aspect ratios available for projectors. Different aspect ratios may cause different reconstruction performance. This research focuses on analysis and solutions to reconstruction errors caused by different aspect ratios in structured light systems. The reasons behind the wavy noise and the variations rebuilt in the various aspect ratios were discussed and investigated. In this study, look-up-table (LUT) calibration method was proposed to correct the errors caused by aspect ratios. The experimental results show that with proposed method, the reconstruction performance can be improved significantly.

articleTitle: Free-Space Optical (FSO) Link for Different Transmission Schemes Influenced By Atmospheric Turbulence with Pointing Errors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Free-space optical (FSO) communication presents a promising solution for high-speed wireless communication, particularly in scenarios where traditional wired or radio frequency-based solutions are impractical or inefficient. However, FSO links are susceptible to Atmospheric Turbulence-Induced Fading (ATIF), weather conditions and pointing errors, which can significantly degrade the channel performance. This paper compares the effectiveness of three transmission schemes - On-Off Keying (OOK), Differential Phase Shift Keying (DPSK), and Binary Phase Shift Keying (BPSK) by analyzing their impact on the maximum data transfer rate (channel capacity), throughput, and overall connection stability. The combined channel state is modeled considering the effects of atmospheric turbulence, weather conditions, and pointing errors. The probability density function of the channel is modeled through gamma-gamma distribution and mathematical analytical closed-form expression for the ergodic channel capacity is derived based on Meijer-G function.

articleTitle: Stain the Phony Brains: Generating Synthetic Different Medical Images Modalities Using Latent Diffusion Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Medical image synthesis is gaining popularity using generative models. latent diffusion models have recently shown promise in producing remarkably life-like representations of items. However, their ability to produce medical imagery has not yet been investigated. We investigate the possibility of latent diffusion models for the synthesis of different medical modalities. Initially, we create MRI images of the brains using a pre-trained DALLE-3 model given an input text prompt. Second, we create synthetic images and use 2300 MRI and 1300 CT images to train a stable diffusion model. Through a qualitative study, we assess the synthetic image data by having two impartial specialists MRI and CT modalities to classify randomly selected samples from the created data as authentic (real), fraudulent (phony), or unclear. Findings show that images produced using the diffusion model can convey qualities that are otherwise highly specific to certain medical conditions in MRI and CT modalities. This paper aims to introduce diffusion models rather than state-of-the-art generative models like Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and provide impetus for the medical image synthesis research community to investigate their possibilities.

articleTitle: A Smart Surveillance and Clocking System for Real-Time Monitoring of the Farm Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The commercial farming sector is plagued by farm attacks, theft of livestock and employee clocking fraud. The majority of surveillance systems currently in use are ineffective in detecting time fraud and unauthorized intrusions. These problems lead to the loss of significant assets and jeopardise the safety of the farm employers and employees. Using advanced gait recognition and unsupervised machine learning (ML) technologies, this study developed a highly accurate, smart clocking and surveillance system to monitor employees and send real-time notifications when an intrusion is detected.

articleTitle: Determination Stenosis from Coronary Stretch Images for CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Coronary artery stenosis, one of the most common heart diseases, is diagnosed by a human, which is a time-consuming and labor-intensive process. Therefore, the diagnosis of coronary artery stenosis is desired to be automated, and deep learning has shown great promise in this regard. In this study, we propose two deep learning models based on coronary artery multi-planar reconstruction (MPR) images from contrast CT images: one inputs each extracted individual coronary artery image (Indiv), and the other inputs an aggregate projected view (APV). The model that used APV images exhibited a maximum F1-score of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.779\pm 0.024$</tex>.

articleTitle: Parasitic Transistor with Hole Injection Current Modeling of AlGaN/GaN Ridge HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The parasitic transistor of embedded source field plate of AlGaN/GaN ridge HEMTs (known as gate injection transistors) with abrupt drain current increase by the gate hole injection current have been characterized with our dedicated test structures including the geometries and temperature variations. Accurate simulations with the model can improve fast and high- power circuit design.

articleTitle: Depth Estimation with Tilted Optics Using Split Color Filter Aperture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Camera-based depth estimation methods are useful for various automobile applications. For example, depth estimation methods based on stereo cameras triangulate the depth between objects and cameras. However, they are susceptible to baseline distortion owing to vibrations, aging, and thermal expansion. On the contrary, depth estimation methods based on a monocular camera, such as depth-from-defocus, use a focusing mechanism or spectroscopic optics to calculate the depth from the difference of defocus images. However, because the change in sharpness, which is the inverse of defocus, is slightly in the depth direction, it is unsuitable for deep-range estimation. Therefore, we are developing depth-estimation methods that use a monocular camera with special focus images obtained through tilted optics, which have no baseline distortion problem and have a deep estimation range. When tilted optics are used, the plane of sharp focus (POF) appears tilted, while the depth of field (DOF) lies and increases toward the depth direction. Moreover, to allow for the use of only one image-sensor, a one-shot, we studied a depth estimation method using tilted optics with two different aperture sizes for each color wavelength by introducing concentric color filter apertures. However, as with conventional methods, the Gaussian sharpness model does not strictly fit to the actual sharpness, resulting in reduced estimation accuracy. In this study, we propose a method for high-speed and high-accuracy depth estimation that involves adding a split color filter aperture to a tilted optic and using a different sharpness model for each DOF side.

articleTitle: Automatic Phase Correction of Microwave Power Transmitter Array Using Nature-Inspired Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This paper presents an automated phase correction method designed for array antennas in Microwave Power Transfer (MPT) systems. Automated phase correction plays a crucial role in optimizing the performance of MPT systems by maximizing the transmitting power towards a specified direction. Our proposed approach utilizes the Global Best-guided Firefly Algorithm (GbFA), a nature-inspired optimization algorithm, to compute the optimal phase configuration of a transmitting array. Through numerical simulations, we demonstrate that the proposed phase correction method using the GbFA effectively delivers maximum power to wireless sensor nodes in MPT scenarios. This research contributes to improving the efficiency and reliability of MPT systems and offers a promising solution for enhancing power transfer in wireless communication networks.

articleTitle: The Geometrical Bayes Theorem and Probabilistic Prediction of Next Global Pandemic
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The recent Corona virus 2019 and Monkeypox 2022 diseases, have manifested the fully unpredictable character of global pandemics as to time and geography where the outbreak begins. Despite of that, the statistics that have leave these pandemics can be taken as a pattern by which exists a probability of continuation of more global pandemics in future. This paper presents an approach based at a fully geometrical concept in conjunction to conditional probabilities. In concrete the Bayes theorem is considered. In this manner, number of infections versus time of a global pandemic can be seen as sides of a trapezoid. The sides of involved geometry can be condition for each other. From this, the peaks can be estimated and the total number of infection can be approximately predicted. Based at data of Corona virus 2019, the next peak of a possible next global pandemic has been predicted. Errors are basically attached on the time estimation of each wave in a finite sequence. Considering the highest peak of 4M infections seen in January 2022, the highest peak for next pandemic might to be ranking between 3M and 7M of infections.

articleTitle: An Optimized Voltage Scaling Circuit for Increasing the Linearity and Input Voltage Range of Voltage to Time Converter Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Voltage-to-time converters (VTCs) employing delay lines demonstrate nonlinearity in the correlation between input voltage and output time. Although selecting a more linear segment helps alleviate nonlinearity, it diminishes the usable input voltage range of the VTC. Furthermore, chip process variations lead to output time drift in the VTC, posing challenges in accurately quantifying input voltage. A voltage scaling circuit, composed of voltage followers, is employed as the input stage of delay lines to provide a bias and voltage gain for reshaping the input voltage of the VTC. This approach not only improves the linearity of the VTC but also extends the input voltage range to achieve nearly rail-to-rail swing. A comparative analysis based on the simulation results, conducted using the UMC 0.18um process, demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Novel Synthetic L-Shaped Array Design for DOA Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: In this paper, a novel synthetic L-shaped array(SLA) is presented for direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation by applying synthetic aperture technique to L-shaped array. We introduce a novel moving sampling strategy, which is easy to implement and significantly enlarges the 2D difference coarray region. The enhanced degrees of freedom and innovative design of SLA contribute to the successful attainment of precise DOA estimation results.

articleTitle: Web Portal Validation Model by Digital Signature and ISO 27002 to Reduce Private Credentials Theft for Phishing Attacks to Financial Sector Customers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Phishing attacks increase by 46% since 2018, mainly affecting the financial sector with losses on average of $3.66 million during 2019. The poor validation procedures of legitimate websites and the carefree aptitude of users in the face of this type of attack have generated their proliferation. The proposed model is divided into the phases of analysis, design, development, experimentation and monitoring; in which the necessary tools are selected, the system architecture is designed considering the criteria of effectiveness, performance, functionality, security and perception of usefulness; It is developed in three layers: backend, middleware, and frontend. The data transfer between the layers implemented the concepts of digital signature in the use of the hash algorithm, asymmetric key and QR codes updated at time intervals. The validation process was carried out using a sample of 106 active users of financial institutions, 100 QR codes, 7 stress loads and in accordance with the ISO 27002 standard. The model reduced the theft of confidential information by 88.87% in an interval of 3 to 6 seconds in the validation process with 100% effectiveness. Likewise, it obtained a 100% satisfaction rate and risk management according to ISO 27002 covered the main inherent risks related to sniffing, QR code spoofing, unauthorized access, cessation of operations and increased latency in the validation process.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Perform an Automated Validation of Radar Emulation Platform Using Qualification Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Automation has long been a widely used term in the technological society and it is currently one of the most in-demand skills. Micro-controllers, on the other hand, are an interesting emerging technology, particularly in the automotive industry where they can be highly valuable. When used in safety-critical applications, automotive microcontrollers undergo a lengthy development cycle of around 3–5 years before they are produced. However, with the increasing demand for applications such as ADAS (Advanced Driver Assistance System), this long gap between product development and production is not ideal for manufacturers. Therefore, any level of automation during any stage of the development cycle is highly desirable. A Radar Emulation Platform is an innovative solution that involves programming the ADAS functional blocks of a Micro-Controller into an FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Array) and using it in real applications. This enables the end customer to utilize these functional blocks before the production of the actual Micro-Controller, which can save more than a year or two in development time. However, before delivering such a platform to the end-user, it must undergo thorough validation to ensure its functionality, which itself can be a time-consuming task. This paper describes a unique and highly automated validation method for such a platform that enables manufacturers to save time for delivery. The method involves automated execution of hundreds of tests to validate the functional blocks, automated data integrity checks for every test, and control of external hardware for driving data. This framework is crucial because the emulation platform is developed in parallel with the microcontroller design and will have many design releases from time-to-time. Therefore, each release must be validated, and the use of an automated framework will significantly save time. Furthermore, this framework is not just beneficial for manufacturers but also for end-customers who can use it to see the results of their application. The level of automation of this validation method makes it an efficient and reliable way to validate the functionality of the Radar Emulation Platform.

articleTitle: Icosahedral CNN for DoA Estimation of EM Wave Sources Arriving Spherical Antenna Array Incorporating the Impact of Mutual Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Spherical antenna array (SAA) is usually employed anytime hemispherical scan coverage is needed, because it generates the same level of directivity in all scan angles. It is applicable in satellite communications, vehicular technology, and aerospace. Hence, the direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation of electromagnetic (EM) waves impinging an SAA with undefined mutual coupling requires academic and industry attention. This paper presents a method for DoA estimation of EM waves via icosahedral convolution neural network (CNN) over steered response power with phase transform power map calculated from EM waves arriving SAA. Icosahedral CNN exhibits equal variation to 60 rotational icosahedral symmetries, representing an appreciable approximates continuous space approximates of spherical rotations, and implementable by the general 2D convolutional layers, exhibiting smaller cost of computation than spherical CNNs. Furthermore, as against the fully connected layers following icosahedral convolutions, soft-argmax function, which is a differential form of the popular argmax function, is employed. This make it possible to compute DoA in form of regression, which represents the convolutional layers output in form of probability distribution. Numerical experimental results shows that the proposed method with fitting equal variation of the problem perform better than the previous methods, in terms of robustness, lower cost of computation, and a root mean square errors of localization lesser than 11 degree, even in harsh environments.

articleTitle: A Robust ADE-CN-RPIM Meshless Algorithm for Modeling Debye Dispersive Meduim
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This paper investigates a novel single-field auxiliary difference equation radial point interpolation meshless method (ADE-RPIM) for simulating electromagnetic behavior in dispersive media by using the Crank-Nicolson (CN) scheme. The ADE technique is used to investigate both electric field intensity and electric displacement vector in dispersive materials in the proposed method. Applying the CN scheme to Faraday's law yields new equations that exclude magnetic fields. A two-dimensional cavity filled with Debye dispersive substance displays the efficiency and accuracy of the suggested ADE-CN-RPIM method. We compare numerical outcomes to the ones obtained using the conventional ADE-CN-FDTD approach.

articleTitle: Clickbait Chronicles: Unmasking the Student Exploitation Scheme Through Social Engineering Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This research explores the exploitation of students at universities through the use of clickbaiting strategies. The study adopts a social engineering paradigm to explore the psychological, sociological, and technological elements involved in the Clickbait Chronicles at Universities. The data suggest that clickbaiters are exploiting students' vulnerabilities, such as their curiosity, emotions, and demand for immediate knowledge. The study also indicated that students at universities are particularly susceptible to clickbaiting attacks because of their dependency on mobile devices and their low awareness of social engineering.

articleTitle: Atmospheric Pressure Energy Storage: Analysis of a Novel Potential Energy Storage Concept
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This paper introduces a novel energy storage concept: Atmospheric Pressure Energy Storage (APES), a mechanical method that leverages potential energy. APES operates based on the ubiquitous atmospheric pressure, which exerts a significant quasi-static force on quasi-vacuum spaces, making it an innovative and reliable energy storage solution. Starting with its fundamental principles, the paper details the system's formulas and evaluates APES's performance through comprehensive simulations. Unlike traditional systems, APES is unaffected by geographical orientation and offers direction-independent setup, stable voltage control, and scalable storage arrays. Its simple installation, non-degrading capacity, and environmentally friendly nature further enhance its appeal. Moreover, this paper provides a comparative analysis between APES and solid gravity energy storage (SGES), underscoring the unique advantages of APES. This work highlights APES as a transformative solution in the energy storage landscape.

articleTitle: Algebraic-Based Velocity Profiling and Path Tracking of a Legged Robot: A Single Leg Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The trajectory control of legged robots has been a challenging aspect in the field of robotics due to its complexity and trajectory errors are likely to occur as a result of the legged robot operating in 12 degrees of freedom. Current motion control approaches require a full knowledge of the dynamic of the system, and solutions are often found using optimisation tools. This work proposes a different approach: it studies the application of an algebraic approach that considers only the kinematic of the robot, and it can be extended to any configuration within certain constraints. To this end, we consider the velocities of the leg in the Cartesian space and the motion approach is formulated on the configuration space. Our approach is tested using one robotic leg, showing encourages results according to tracking errors, but the approach can be easily extended to 4 or 6 legged robots.

articleTitle: A Personalized E-Mail Category Generation Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: When e-mail users wish to manage4 their e-mails, they need to read the e-mail content to identify the e-mail properties, and then classify and manage the e-mails themselves. However, large numbers of e-mails become very time-consuming to manually classify. Previous studies have therefore developed various related e-mail classification techniques. However, users often send private e-mails, and their contents will mainly consist of implicit personal life experiences and expertise. Existing classification techniques based on specified fields thus lack accuracy when it comes to personal e-mail classification. That is, based on personal knowledge, life experiences and other factors, the required e-mail categories of each e-mail user might be different. This paper therefore proposes a Personalized E-Mail Category Generation model to generate personalized e-mail categories allowing users to efficiently manage their own e-mails. In the proposed model, semantic analysis technology is used to analyze and extract critical features from e-mail content. Based on these critical features, clustering technology is employed to distinguish e-mail groups and generate corresponding names as personalized e-mail categories. Therefore, the proposed method can automatically generate personalized e-mail categories to assist e-mail users in managing their private e-mails.

articleTitle: An Overview of Various Applications of Ordinal Patterns in Data Analysis and Mathematical Statistics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Ordinal pattern analysis has a wide spectrum of applications which a novice to the field can hardly keep track of. The applications range from entropy concepts to estimators of the Hurst parameter and also include various dependence measures. In the present article, we give an overview of the applications we are aware of and we provide the reader with literature to further deepen their knowledge.

articleTitle: OpenAI's GPT-3/ChatGPT: Suggests & Correct
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: OpenAI's ChatGPT is a GPT-3-based chatbot that has been optimized through supervised and reinforcement learning methodologies. The training data includes information about internet phenomena and programming languages like Python. However, ChatGPT has limitations, such as over-optimized reward models and limited training data from 2021. This study tests the effectiveness of ChatGPT in syntax auto-correction and output generation from Python code libraries.

articleTitle: The Work on the Application of Electrical Machines and the Project Method in a Public University of Peru
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The purpose of this research is to present an improved project method and the results obtained in its use for the application work of the electrical machines course of an electronic engineering program of the Pedro Ruiz Gallo National University of Lambayeque in Peru. Previously, from 2013 to 2018, the project method was used, and based on these experiences, a proj ect method was prepared with greater detail of the activities and deliverables in each phase of the method, the results are better information, planning and organization by part of the students and a better evaluation by the facilitator, who acts as a referee and not as a coach as in traditional vocational training. The improved project method that has been applied in the 2019–11 semester and completed the validation in the 2023 semesters, due to the COVID 19 quarantine in the years 2020 to 2022, no real application work was carried out. In order to train professionals with new skills, vocational training must be innovated with new teaching-learning modes, such as the project method. The projects carried out in 2019–11 gave 4 very good projects: Automotive alternator as direct current generator, DC generator based on a DC motor, Construction of a windshield wiper system, Construction of a single-phase induction motor; 2 good projects and 5 regular projects.

articleTitle: Enhancing Large Language Model Performance with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: A Comprehensive Study on Q&A, Summarization, and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) has shown great potential in enhancing the alignment of Large Language Models (LLMs) with human preferences. In this study, we introduce a effective approach aimed at improving the performance of LLMs in tasks such as question-answering, Summarization, and classification. Our methodology incorporates RLHF into LLMs, facilitating better adherence to human expectations and resulting in superior task performance. We detail the implementation of RLHF within the LLM architecture, with a focus on leveraging reward signals derived from human feedback to direct model updates. This methodology encompasses data generation, Supervised Finetuning, reward model training, and reinforcement learning with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed RLHF-augmented LLMs outperform baseline models, attesting to their efficacy in achieving higher performance while maintaining human-aligned behaviour. Notably, we observe a 5 to 15 percent improvement in outcomes using the RLHF implementation in LLMs. The findings of this study have significant implications for the advancement of more accurate, efficient, and human-centric language models.

articleTitle: A Mathematical Model of Asymmetric Encryption Based on Linear Diophantine Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: in this paper, an information cryptography system is presented as asymmetric encryption based on the linear Diophantine equation ax + by=c. This system consists of two parts for encrypting plain text. In the first, the plain text is encrypted using a linear equation repeatedly with two public keys that were previously generated. As for the second, encrypted cipher texts are derived from the first part and encrypted again through the use of a proposed equation by another two public keys, which led to overcoming complexity in the related works by setting precedent for complexity generating keys and increasing the number of keys with the increase in the number of plain texts to be encrypted. Thus, this system provides a simple and, at the same time, more secure system, as analyzed in this paper.

articleTitle: Enhancing Generalization and Convergence in Neural Networks through a Dual-Phase Regularization Approach with Excitatory-Inhibitory Transition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Overfitting and slow convergence represent common hurdles encountered during the training of deep neural networks (DNNs). While conventional regularization methods like dropout and weight decay can alleviate these challenges to some extent, they may prove insufficient for more intricate models and hardware implementations. In this study, we introduce a novel dual-phase regularization approach aimed at enhancing the generalization and accelerating the convergence of neural networks. Diverging from conventional dropout methods, which randomly deactivate neurons or connections during training, our approach incorporates an excitatory-inhibitory transition mechanism. This mechanism selectively identifies large synaptic weights surpassing a predetermined threshold and converts them to an opposite phase state based on predefined flipping rules prior to the commencement of each training batch. Specifically, these pre-processed synaptic weights revert to their original values and are then updated using gradients calculated from the pre-processed DNN. This excitatory-inhibitory transition effectively facilitates an interconversion process between states of high and low impedance. Through experimentation on the CIFAR-10 benchmark dataset, we demonstrate the superior convergence speed of our approach compared to other regularization techniques, while concurrently maintaining comparable generalization performance. These findings suggest a promising avenue for enhancing the training efficiency and efficacy of neural networks in practical applications.

articleTitle: LLMOps: Definitions, Framework and Best Practices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Operationalizing large language models is unlike traditional AI solutioning. As the vestiges of the MLOps paradigm serve as a reminder of the sophistication that surfaces at scale, Generative AI, while mitigating a few of those challenges, brings a few of its own. This is where LLMOps (Large Language Model Operations) comes into the picture. LLMOps is a subset of FMOps (Foundation Model Operations) that builds on the principles of MLOps (Machine Learning Operations) and helps enterprises deploy, monitor, and retrain their LLMs seamlessly. This paper provides a comprehensive definition of LLMOps and a robust framework and highlights best practices accrued through our experience building solutions in different domains. Finally, this work attempts to provide guidance for AI practitioners who want to operationalize their GenAl applications seamlessly.

articleTitle: Control of Wind Turbines Operating at Significantly Variable Wind Speeds Over Time
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: In the present paper, the operation of high-power wind turbines of the order of mega-watts (MW), is analysed at significantly variable wind speeds over time. Experimental data from a wind turbine operating in the Dobrogea region are processed, at a higher sampling frequency of measurements. The current operating condition is investigated from an efficiency viewpoint and compared with an optimized controlled setting, in which the electric generator power is controlled dependent on the wind speed value. We find that wind speed sampling frequency is an important factor impacting control quality, while the improved control is mandatory for maximal operation efficiency.

articleTitle: Neutralizing Effects of a Disturbance on Volatge in an Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This article presents a proposed plan to counteract the impact of various disturbances on the voltage of the system in the microgrid of an island. Network elements and equipment are initially simulated based on given values, and then the system under investigation is analyzed in operational mode, dissecting and interpreting network parameters. Several potential errors in the network are implemented for a more precise examination of their effects on the experimental microgrid. Based on the results obtained from different disturbances in the microgrid under study, a scheme is introduced to neutralize the error effects and restore the network to the desired range. Finally, the proposed plan's influence and its results on the disturbances occurring in the examined system are evaluated. The simulation section demonstrates the effectiveness of the suggested strategy on the microgrid of Alborg, Denmark, placed in island mode.

articleTitle: Design a Rectifier with High Sensitivity and High Efficiency for RF Energy Harvesting Applications: Fundamental, Development, and Future-A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting utilizes ubiquitous RF signals, offering broader applicability compared to other sources like solar or geothermal energy. RF rectifiers, like Dickson and cross-coupled types, efficiently convert RF power to direct current (DC) power, crucial for IoT devices. Power conversion efficiency (PCE) and Sensitivity are key parameters in RF rectifier design. Higher PCE ensures efficient energy conversion, reducing heat generation and extending device lifespan. Higher sensitivity enables reliable long-distance power transmission, which is vital in wireless communication systems and medical applications. Our paper explores RF to DC energy conversion, focusing on Dickson and cross-coupled rectifiers, delving into principles and advanced techniques. Additionally, we discussed performance characteristics and potential applications of recent energy harvesting technologies to provide guidance for future research.

articleTitle: Improvement Research of Zero-DCE-Based Algorithm for Low-Light Style Transfer in Generative Cartoon GANs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Among the rapidly developed generative artificial intelligence, CartoonGAN is attracting a lot of attention as it can overcome the limitations of Cartoon production occurring in fields such as Cartoon and animation. CartoonGAN has a problem of not properly preserving the subject shape and edge of a low-light image. To this end, research should be conducted to recover the shape of the subject and improve the structural features of the image through the adjustment of brightness and noise. Therefore, in this study, CartoonGAN, a Cartoon style image generation model using deep learning, proposes a method of applying Zero-DCE to the pre-processing process to overcome the limitations arising from low-light image processing. Through this process, the brightness and color of a low-light image are improved without a reference image. The performance of the proposed algorithm was evaluated through image quality evaluation indicators such as a peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and a structural similarity index (SSIM). The experimental results showed that the proposed algorithm is effective in improving the performance of CartoonGAN. In addition, it was confirmed that the proposed algorithm effectively improved the brightness of the image through the measurement of the brightness improvement, and a performance evaluation for the recovery of subject information was also performed by introducing a new evaluation method. These results show that CartoonGAN can be improved and effectively applied to low-light image processing. Therefore, this study contributes to the development of image generation technology based on deep learning and presents an important direction to provide high performance in real-world application fields.

articleTitle: Quantized Energies from Finite Chain of Dirac-Delta Impulses at MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: A formalism that associates inputs of form Dirac-Delta to quantized energy at MIMO systems is developed. Thus when Dirac-Delta inputs enter to system, errors at the measurement of observables can be crucial to trigger energy quantization. Thus, the case when photon energy is perceived as a kind of error then it allows to system to exhibit quantization of energy. The developed theory agrees well to well-known dispersion relation. The propagator known in quantum electrodynamics as the one that guarantees the momentum-energy conservation is demonstrated that can be represented as a chain of Dirac-Delta functions. Simulations have shown that in polynomial MIMO systems such as atoms, it is possible to extract the poles of system that to some extent would denote the eigenstates of system energy.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning-based Short- Term Prediction Model for a Solar Plant: A South African case study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: The research presented in this paper examines and develops a machine learning-based model to predict the hourly output of a rooftop solar installation in a petrochemical industrial facility in South Africa. This research attempts to thoroughly examine the factors impacting solar energy generation and then create a reliable predictive model for solar power. This work uses machine learning to produce an accurate and dependable model to increase the effectiveness of energy management systems. It was established that solar power output and efficiency depend on various environmental factors and the year's season. The results show RMSE values of 4.30, 4.22, and 11.89 for the 1D CNN, LSTM and hybrid CNN-LSTM models, respectively.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Node Authentication Algorithm for Mobile Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: MANET is an intriguing technology that can be used by first responders at disaster sites or soldiers in the field to provide communications in the absence of fixed infrastructure. Because of its Ad Hoc capabilities, MANET has grown quickly in recent years, making it a popular target for cybercriminals. This begs the question of how to reap the benefits of MANETs without raising the stakes in terms of security. MANETs are vulnerable to a number of issues, including insecure communication, cooperative nature, lack of a central point, mobility, wireless links, limited power sources, and unclear defense lines. Nodes have unrestricted mobility and self-organization freedom. Verifying the identity of nodes through authentication is necessary to guarantee the security of communication and data transmission. This research study proposed a Node Authentication (NA) algorithm using the Record and Trust-based Detection Technique (RTBD) and Reputation-Based Scheme (RBS) to secure communication and prevent unauthorized or malicious nodes from joining the network by allowing nodes to identify themselves by verifying their identities before joining and leaving the network. Simulation results will be presented in the future to show the superior performance of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: Detecting Fileless Malware on Windows with ATT&CK: A Practical Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This paper delves into the field of fileless malware (FM), a complicated sort of malware that runs fully in memory and leaves very few traces on the host computer. Our focus is on detecting such elusive threats on windows systems, particularly those that use administrative tools like PowerShell and Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) to execute and propagate. To identify these attacks, we present a viable approach based on the Adversarial Tactics, Techniques, and Common Knowledge (ATT&CK) paradigm. Our objective is to investigate detection strategies that can dispel myths about the technological complexity of FM. The results show that our technique is effective at identifying and aiding intrusion assessment, adding to the overall goal of information security. This paper is a helpful resource for cybersecurity professionals wanting to improve their defenses against FM.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Double Square FSS for Sub 6G Applications Using ML Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Frequency Selective Surfaces (FSS) play a very critical role now-a-days in electromagnetic engineering, which enables precise control of electromagnetic wave propagation for various applications. This article explores the integration of Machine Learning (ML) algorithms to optimize the structure to achieve enhanced performance and efficiency for Sub 6G applications (6 GHz and 2.4 GHz). The Double Square Frequency Selective Surface (DS-FSS) consists of two distinct layers of square shaped periodic patterns. The substrate used is RT Duroid 5880 which has a dielectric constant of 2.2 with a width of 1.6 mm for better characteristics. The periodicity of the unit cell is 20 mm x 20 mm which makes it isotropic and polarization insensitive. This configuration provides greater flexibility in tailoring the overall frequency response compared to single layer FSS. A comprehensive data set (approx. 5000) has been prepared by simulating the electromagnetic responses from the Equivalent Circuit Model (ECM) which are fed to the ML algorithm to extract the features and build the regression model and to estimate the optimal parameters. The ML algorithms used are Linear Regression and Random Forest. These are then validated against the electromagnetic simulations using HFSS Software. Two stop bands, one at 2.4 GHz and the other at 6.3 GHz and one pass band at 3.8 GHz has been achieved. Shielding Effectiveness of about 49 dB is achieved at 2.4 GHz and about 57 dB is achieved at 6.3 GHz. The angular stability of 0° to 80°, with a stable bandwidth, is also achieved by the proposed design which is better than the existing works.

articleTitle: Drones Detection and Classification Based on RF Signal Pre-Processing Combing with Convolution Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: In recent years, the development of science and technology has led to the increasing popularity of small unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) such as drones. With the convenience of use and the decreasing cost, the demand for using drones in civilian applications, from personal purposes such as filming and aerial photography to economic purposes such as transportation, will continue to increase. However, this will allow anyone using drones to access geographical areas that were previously inaccessible before the existence of drones. This will certainly cause many difficulties for the monitoring and management of restricted areas. In this study, we propose a solution for the detection and classification of drones based on RF signal preprocessing combined with a convolution neural network. The results of the proposed model verified on the real dataset achieved drones detection rate of 99% and drones classification rate of 84%.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Characteristics of Gradient Descent and Non-Gradient Descent-Based Algorithms in Neural Network Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: In this paper, a comparative analysis of optimization algorithms for artificial neural networks widely used in the fields of machine learning and deep learning was conducted. Beyond the conventional backpropagation algorithm utilizing gradient descent, we investigated the characteristics of various optimization methods for neural networks, including alternative non-gradient descent approaches such as the Forward-Forward (FF) algorithm and Genetic Algorithm (GA). Our analysis revealed diverse performances of each algorithm contingent upon the characteristics of the image dataset and the problem at hand. Furthermore, by scrutinizing the features and limitations of each algorithm, we provided considerations for practical applications. These findings offer crucial guidelines for selecting the optimal weight update methods tailored to specific problem domains.

articleTitle: The Method of Verification of Sphere Kinematics by Two Mouse Image Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: In the past, omni-directional wheels, including omni-rollers, have been studied. The sphere has attracted attention as a shape with better running and overweight characteristics than this. Because of its excellent symmetry, it has been used as a wheel in omni-directional moving mechanisms. Spherical robots driven by two constrained rollers have been studied extensively, not only to derive their kinematics but also to study their validation methods. In this study, we propose a new method for verifying sphere kinematics, in which the rotational motion of spheres driving two rollers by two mouse sensors and used for estimation calculations.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of the Lossless Data Compression Methods for Unsparsed Tabular Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: This paper conducts a comparative analysis of the impact of unsparsing by data scaling on lossless data compression methods. The most commonly used data compression algorithms such as gzip, zlib, bzip2, and lzma are tested by their compression efficiency in unsparsed datasets by the performance metrics such as compression time, decompression time, and compression ratio for both the original and scaled datasets. Five different data scaling techniques are investigated to transform the original data into unsparsed data such as min-max, robust, absolute max, standardization, and normalization. Our research reveals relationships between data scaling methodologies and compression performance, with disparities in compression efficiency and computational complexity. Fur-thermore, we investigate the effects of scaling on compression ratio and provide results for improving the understanding of the factors that influence lossless data compression methods for non-sparse tabular data.

articleTitle: Unified Structure to Generate Sparsity-Inducing Regularizers for Enhanced Low-Rank Matrix Completion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Applying half-quadratic optimization to loss functions can generate the associated regularizers, while these reg-ularizers are usually not able to give a sparse solution. To address it, we put forth an unified structure to produce sparsity-promoting regularizers with closed-form proximity operators. In addition, three commonly-used loss functions are adopted in our structure to generate the corresponding sparsity-inducing regu-larizers, which are then employed as nonconvex rank surrogates to achieve enhanced low-rank matrix completion. Furthermore, algorithms with convergence guarantees are developed, and numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of our methods in terms of recovery performance and runtime.

articleTitle: Preserving the Stability of Microgrid with Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Increasing the penetration of distributed generation units in the distribution system has made it possible to operate distributed generation systems in islanded mode. However, maintaining network parameters, especially network voltage within the desired range, is one of the most important actions during microgrid operation. Due to various disturbances in the microgrid, it faces various challenges. This article attempts to protect the network against various faults by placing protective relays on power keys and ensuring the stability of the microgrid by controlling the voltage of the busbars in the microgrid over a short period of time, preventing it from being affected by various disturbances. Different data is analyzed through data mining, then assistance is sought from a neural network model as deep learning approach to detect the state of the microgrid, the type of fault, and the lost elements in the network. Finally, with planning and algorithmic compensation, and returning the voltage outside the desired limit, changes are made in the microgrid. To simulate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy, the microgrid of ALBORG, Denmark, in islanded mode, has been utilized.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Stick for Blind Humans Using Artificial Intelligence System and FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Blind people need a means of assistance to help them carry out their daily activities without relying on the people close to them, so the researchers thought of using intelligence methods to make a smart stick that helps them bypass the obstacles they face while walking, the research examined the use of an image as a blind environment in a fuzzy logic system to find a path and avoid obstacles for blind stick. This demonstrates the effectiveness of the fuzzy logic algorithm for the smart stick and ensures the path by performing path behavior and obstacle avoidance to identify the best path for smart stick can access the target and avoidance obstacles. In this paper, one of the methods of artificial intelligence is presented, which is the fuzzy logic of making a smart stick, where an algorithm has been built in the Matlab program to avoid and bypass obstacles and cross safely and then upload a code in FPGA then connect with power supply, flat Vibrator motor, ultrasonic sensor, buzzer that alert when detect an obstacles. The result use of fuzzy logic gives the best results for overcoming obstacles because fuzzy logic depends on the principle of probabilities and the use of the FPGA chip is the best chip from the Arduino and the Raspberry because the FPGA works in parallel with several inputs and sensors. Thus, a smart stick has been designed with artificial intelligence techniques and a FPGA chip with great success.

articleTitle: Comparative Verification of Frequency Fluctuation and Power Efficiency of Wind and Energy Storage Power System caused by Wind Speed Prediction using the Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Network Model and Corrected Autoregressive Model Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: In this study, a bidirectional recurrent neural network (BiRNN) method and a unique method, which is the corrected autoregressive (AR) model, are investigated to predict wind speed one hour ahead. Then, it is applied to a wind power generation system using a redox flow storage battery. The simulation compares frequency fluctuations and power efficiency (Actual electric energy of the prediction method / Wind effective electric energy) in the simulation using wind speed prediction data from the two methods. The two characteristics of the corrected AR model are that the order of AIC (Akaike Information Criterion) is fixed at 15 to eliminate blank periods, and the one-hour average value of the difference between past one-hour averaged AR model prediction and the actual wind speed is added to the predicted value for one hour ahead. Both the BiRNN model and the corrected AR model results are passed through a low-pass filter to remove variations in the wind speed prediction curve. In addition, we compared and verified the results using 1-minute wind speed data created from 10-minute average wind speed data using a spline interpolation method and actual 1-minute average data. As a result, almost the same results were obtained by using both data. In most cases, frequency fluctuations were within an acceptable range of 0.3 Hz for both methods, and the corrected AR model method had smaller frequency fluctuations and was more energy efficient. Using this system to predict the amount of power that can be supplied one hour later is useful because it does not increase wasteful CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions and allows efficient use of planed wind power system output.

articleTitle: Enhancing EMI Suppressor Designs through Multilayered Magnetic Cores in Toroidal Inductors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: EMI suppressors are passive components typically used to filter high-frequency noise due to their high resistance value. That is usually employed using ferrite material with a higher magnetic loss. This paper introduces a novel approach to fabricating such a device without relying on bulky ferrite materials as the magnetic core. The proposed approach relies on using multilayered materials with high electrical conductivity as the magnetic core. We propose three toroid inductor designs using two customized magnetic materials (A and B) with higher electrical conductivity properties. The first toroid design is based on a single-layer magnetic core, the second on a double-layer magnetic core, and the last on an eight-layer magnetic core. The performance of the single-layered toroid inductor is improved by employing a multi-layered core technique in terms of AC resistance across broadband bandwidth. Notably, the multilayered toroid core exhibits higher resistance across the 5–1175 MHz range as compared to the single-layer design. In addition, Depositing conductive layers like copper onto the multilayered toroids leads to inductors that have multiple resonances. Thus, such an approach allows to control and adjust the operational frequency as needed.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Indoor Positioning System Using Wi-Fi Fingerprinting Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET
abstract: Indoor Positioning System has emerged as an intriguing application in the field of computer networks and IoT. Due to the growth of wireless technology and increment in the number of devices connected with the internet, it has become a paramount to make the proficient applications of computer networks using machine learning and deep learning. Global Positioning System (GPS) is used to navigate and locate places in an outdoor environment but it cannot be used for indoor positioning as GPS signals cannot propagate through walls. Location based services are prone to challenges like non line of sight, attenuation, high complexity, unreliability, adaptability and scalability issue. These challenges are resolved by a variety of machine learning techniques. The Indoor Positioning System uses indoor localization schemes to develop indoor mapping and tracing. We perform Indoor localization in wireless systems using Wi-Fi fingerprinting in which the RSSI data of about 200 Wi-Fi Access Points (WAP) is worked upon to find the definite locations and movements. The Wi-Fi Fingerprinting works in two phases namely offline and online phase. This study aims to provide floor and room classification of an indoor environment.
